name: CI ROCm
display_title: [XLA:GPU] extend runtime offset type to i64 if it might not fit

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] extend runtime offset type to i64 if it might not fit

`EmitClampedIndex` clamps a runtime offset (e.g. a dynamic-slice offset) to
`[0, dim - slice_size]`, but it built the bound constants in the type of the
offset. When `dim - slice_size` does not fit in that signed type, the upper
bound is silently truncated leading to wrong results.

Fix: if a bound does not fit in the offset type, sign-extend the offset to
i64 before clamping. Offsets whose bounds fit (the common case) are emitted
as before.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: [XLA:SPMD] Simplify single-replica flattened-ID index and propagate layouts in decomposer.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:SPMD] Simplify single-replica flattened-ID index and propagate layouts in decomposer.

In single-replica SPMD (`replica_count == 1 && num_partitions > 1`), `replica-id()` is always 0, so the flattened device ID (`replica-id() * num_partitions + partition-id()`) simplifies directly to `partition-id()`. Previously, collective decomposition only folded `replica-id()` to 0 for cross-replica-and-partition groups (emitted by GSPMD), leaving a redundant `replica-id()` multiply-add for flattened-ID groups (emitted by Shardy). Also propagate layouts to all newly created index instructions when decomposing collectives after layout assignment.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1013835361

name: CI ROCm
display_title: Avoid unnecessary heap allocations in HloInstruction::ReplaceAllUsesWithDifferentShape.

head_commit.message:
Avoid unnecessary heap allocations in HloInstruction::ReplaceAllUsesWithDifferentShape.

In the `absl::Span` overload `HloInstruction::ReplaceAllUsesWithDifferentShape(absl::Span<HloInstruction* const>, HloInstruction*)` (`xla/hlo/ir/hlo_instruction.cc`), replace `std::vector<HloInstruction*> users_vector` with `absl::InlinedVector<HloInstruction*, 4> users_vector`. An inline capacity of 4 fits within a single 64-byte cache line on the stack (40 bytes on 64-bit platforms: 4 pointers + 8-byte `InlinedVector` header) and covers typical HLO instruction fanout (1-4 users) without heap allocation while preserving safe iteration when `ReplaceUseWithDifferentShape` mutates `this->users_`.

In the single-argument overload `HloInstruction::ReplaceAllUsesWithDifferentShape(HloInstruction*)`, iterate directly over `users()` without materializing a temporary copy, since `this->users_` is not mutated inside the loop before `users_.Clear()`.

Microbenchmark results (`--benchmark_repetitions=9`, `-c opt`):

| Benchmark | Baseline | Optimized | Delta |
| :--- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `BM_ReplaceAllUsesWithDifferentShape/4` | 294 ns | 211 ns | -28.2% (1.39x) |
| `BM_ReplaceAllUsesWithDifferentShape/16` | 613 ns | 497 ns | -18.9% (1.23x) |

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1005431621

name: CI ROCm
display_title: [XLA] Simplify the identity map in ComputeEpilogueInputToOutputIndexing.

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Simplify the identity map in ComputeEpilogueInputToOutputIndexing.

`ComputeEpilogueInputToOutputIndexing` only ran `Simplify()` while walking a
non-trivial hero->root use chain. When the root *is* the hero, the raw
identity map was returned instead. With size-1 dimensions the two forms
differ structurally (`(d0, d1, d2) -> (0, d1, d2)` vs.
`(d0, d1, d2) -> (d0, d1, d2)`) even though they are semantically equal, so
`IndexingMap::operator==` reports them as different.

The multi-output concatenate emitter compares the epilogue indexing of all
roots and fails with

```
RET_CHECK failure (xla/codegen/emitters/concatenate_kernel_emitter.cc:200)
UseConcatenateFusion should have ensured all roots share the same epilogue indexing
```

for a fusion where one root is `divide(concatenate(...), ...)` and the other
root is a bare `concatenate`, as soon as the shapes contain a size-1
dimension.

Simplify the initial identity map so the result is canonical regardless of
the chain length. Adds a unit test for the indexing analysis and a GPU
emitter lit test with the failing fusion.

Fixes https://github.com/EnzymeAD/Reactant.jl/issues/3681

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1013012065

display_title: Allow deserializing cuDNN graphs compiled for GPUs with fewer SMs

head_commit.message:
Allow deserializing cuDNN graphs compiled for GPUs with fewer SMs

cuDNN's handle-based execution plan deserialization requires an exact match on
`multiProcessorCount`, so AOT plans for a smaller-SM SKU or MIG partition fail
to load on a GPU of the same architecture with more SMs.

To support this, we serialize the target's compute capability, SM count and
cuDNN's `DeviceProperties` JSON into `CudnnThunkProto` at compile time and pass
them to `DnnSupport::DeserializeGraph`. The JSON stays opaque to XLA: when the
target compute capability matches the attached GPU and has fewer SMs,
`CudnnSupport::DeserializeGraph` deserializes the compile-time
`DeviceProperties`, finalizes the plan against those properties via
`graph.set_device_properties()`, and runs warmup on the handle (keeping same-SM
loads on the existing handle path).

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1008122633

name: CI ROCm
display_title: Add module metadata accessors to Executable

head_commit.message:
Add module metadata accessors to Executable

Callers that need the input/output aliasing, the buffer donors, the static device assignment or the entry computation layout of an executable currently read them from the HloModule. That doesn't work for GPU executables that don't keep the module (`embed_hlo_module=false`, and soon loaded AOT executables).

So this change adds `input_output_alias_config()`, `buffer_donor_config()`, `static_device_assignment()` and `entry_computation_layout()` to `Executable`. By default they read from the module, so nothing changes for other backends. `GpuExecutable` overrides them and stores the values at creation time. The aliasing is rebuilt from the output info that is already part of `GpuExecutableProto`. The other values come from the module, the serialized module config, or (with `embed_hlo_module=false`) from the compiler via `GpuExecutable::Params`. The compiler now also passes the partition size that way, so `GpuExecutable::partition_size()` is correct without the module.

This way callers can be migrated to the new accessors in follow-up changes without needing the module.

display_title: Build the HLO module of StreamExecutorExecutable on demand

head_commit.message:
Build the HLO module of StreamExecutorExecutable on demand

StreamExecutorExecutable used to grab the HLO module from its compiled module or executable in the constructor and kept it alive for its whole lifetime. Deserialization also needed the module to get the name, the replica and partition counts and the fingerprint of the executable. That's a problem for XLA:GPU since we want GpuExecutable to build its HLO module only when somebody actually asks for it.

So this change makes StreamExecutorExecutable ask for the module in GetHloModule instead. It also adds an optional StreamExecutorExecutableMetadataProvider interface to xla/pjrt/se, which backends can install to serve the module and the deserialization metadata without a module. The XLA:GPU implementation lives in xla/pjrt/gpu: it lets GpuExecutable build its module on demand, and it reads the metadata of deserialized executables from the serialized GpuExecutableProto. It registers itself with StreamExecutorGpuCompiler when it's linked in. This happens through the GPU compiler registrations, so we don't need any preprocessor conditionals and xla/pjrt/gpu doesn't depend on XLA:GPU executables in other configurations. Without a provider, StreamExecutorExecutable keeps today's module based behaviour.

Right now every StreamExecutorExecutable still has a module, so the results don't change. The tests check that the metadata from the proto matches the metadata from the deserialized module.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Autotune generic Triton fusions over the cost model's top-k configs

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Autotune generic Triton fusions over the cost model's top-k configs

Generic Triton fusions (kind __triton, e.g. from SoftmaxRewriterTriton and
PriorityFusion) keep the cost model's top-1 block-level config and were never
autotuned, even with xla_gpu_fusion_autotune_top_k_configs > 1.

With top-k > 1, ConfigAssignerPass now autotunes them if the fusion
autotuner and the block-level emitter backend are enabled.
BlockLevelEmitterBackend supports them and offers the cost model's top-k
configs, falling back to the pre-existing config if the tiling search fails.

NativeEmitterBackend::GetDefaultConfig and ApplyConfig now reject
unsupported instructions, so a Triton fusion's config can't be silently
replaced with a native one.

With top-k == 1 (the default), compilation output is unchanged.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: [XLA:GPU] Accept float-normalized add combiners in Triton scans and share the check with CanTritonHandleScan.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Accept float-normalized add combiners in Triton scans and share the check with CanTritonHandleScan.

Add `IsAdditiveScanCombiner`. It requires a combiner with two parameters of the output element type whose root is `tuple(x, x)`, where `x` is `add(p0, p1)` or `convert(add(convert(p0), convert(p1)))`. Use it in:

- `EmitScan`, which now accepts the `convert` form. This fixes `bf16` scans on pre-Hopper GPUs (e.g. A100, A6000), where `GpuFloatSupport` normalizes `bf16` `kAdd` and `FloatNormalization` wraps it in `kConvert`s. `EmitScan` now also rejects combiners whose carry differs from the output, because the lowering derives the carry from the output, and combiners whose add operands are not the parameters.
- `CanTritonHandleScan`, which accepted any associative combiner supported by Triton, so `ScanRewriterTriton` could create scan fusions that `EmitScan` rejects (e.g. a max scan). `FusionBlockLevelRewriter` checks the fusion after `FloatNormalization`, so `CanTritonHandleScan` must accept the `convert` form as well.

Make the combiners in `ScanSupportTest` valid `tuple(add, add)` roots, and check the forbid reason in each negative test. Add support tests for non-additive combiners, a device test for the `convert` form, and a lit test that compiles a `bf16` cumulative sum to a Triton scan kernel.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1011625424

unsupported instructions, so a Triton fusion's config can't be silently
replaced with a native one.

display_title: [XLA:SPMD] Simplify single-replica flattened-ID index and propagate layouts in decomposer.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:SPMD] Simplify single-replica flattened-ID index and propagate layouts in decomposer.

In single-replica SPMD (`replica_count == 1 && num_partitions > 1`), `replica-id()` is always 0, so the flattened device ID (`replica-id() * num_partitions + partition-id()`) simplifies directly to `partition-id()`. Previously, collective decomposition only folded `replica-id()` to 0 for cross-replica-and-partition groups (emitted by GSPMD), leaving a redundant `replica-id()` multiply-add for flattened-ID groups (emitted by Shardy). Also propagate layouts to all newly created index instructions when decomposing collectives after layout assignment.

display_title: Fix 32-bit integer overflow when sharding large iota and arange arrays.

head_commit.message:
Fix 32-bit integer overflow when sharding large iota and arange arrays.

When sharding an `iota` (such as `jnp.arange`) across multiple devices, XLA's SPMD partitioner previously computed each shard's starting offset in 32-bit signed integers before converting to the output type. For ranges whose shard size or starting offset exceeded 2^31 - 1, this overflowed and produced negative offsets even for 64-bit outputs.

Build sharded `iota` offsets directly in the `iota` element type via `MakePartitionOffsets`.

Fixes https://github.com/jax-ml/jax/issues/35896

name: CI ROCm
display_title: Fix grouped convolution partitioning with partially replicated sharding.

head_commit.message:
Fix grouped convolution partitioning with partially replicated sharding.

When a grouped convolution has contracting dimensions partitioned with partial replication across other mesh axes, PartitionConvolutionWithSpatialDimensionHaloExchangeOnLHS/RHS previously attempted to handle spatial halo exchange even when no spatial dimensions were partitioned. In doing so, it all-reduced over all devices in the mesh, multiplying the result by the size of the replicated axis.

We now reject partitioned non-spatial dimensions in the spatial halo exchange handlers and return nullptr from spatial halo exchange when no spatial dimensions are partitioned, allowing the convolution to fall through to contracting dimension partitioning. This restricts the spatial halo exchange all-reduce to only reduce across partitioned_spatial_dims instead of all devices in the mesh.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1013501847

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Remove disabled autotune backends when no backend list is set.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Remove disabled autotune backends when no backend list is set.

`ConfigAssignerPass::GetEnabledBackends` removes disabled backends from `xla_gpu_experimental_autotune_backends` and passes the result on as an allowlist, where an empty list means all backends. DebugOptions that don't start from `DefaultDebugOptionsIgnoringFlags()`, e.g. ones serialized before it populated the list, can leave the list empty. Then nothing is removed, and disabled backends stay enabled, e.g. `TENSOR_IR` without `xla_gpu_experimental_enable_tensor_ir`.

Populate an empty list with all backends, like the defaults do, before removing the disabled ones. All existing rules (binary libraries, emitters, Triton, TensorIR) then apply to an empty list too.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: Allow deserializing cuDNN graphs compiled for GPUs with fewer SMs

head_commit.message:
Allow deserializing cuDNN graphs compiled for GPUs with fewer SMs

cuDNN's handle-based execution plan deserialization requires an exact match on
`multiProcessorCount`, so AOT plans for a smaller-SM SKU or MIG partition fail
to load on a GPU of the same architecture with more SMs.

To support this, we serialize cuDNN's `DeviceProperties` JSON into
`CudnnThunkProto` at compile time and pass it to `DnnSupport::DeserializeGraph`.
When the target architecture matches the attached GPU and has fewer SMs,
`CudnnSupport::DeserializeGraph` deserializes the compile-time
`DeviceProperties`, finalizes the plan against those properties via
`graph.set_device_properties()`, and runs warmup on the handle (keeping same-SM
loads on the existing handle path).

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1008122633

head_commit.message:
Don't require an HloModule for RunAsync VLOGs

PjRtStreamExecutorRawLoadedExecutable::Execute logs the module name before and after RunAsync via `Executable::module()`, which CHECK-fails when the executable doesn't hold an HloModule. So turning on `VLOG(1)` crashes the GPU execute path for such executables.

display_title: Reject deserialization of early-exit GPU executables

head_commit.message:
Reject deserialization of early-exit GPU executables

For executables compiled with `xla_early_exit_with_layouts`, `StreamExecutorExecutable::SerializeExecutable` only writes the compile options. `StreamExecutorExecutable::Deserialize` turned that back into an executable without a `CompiledModule`, which hits the `CHECK` in the constructor that requires an `HloModule`. So loading such a serialized executable crashed the process.

Loading early-exit executables isn't supported anyway (`CommonPjRtClient::LoadInternal` rejects them), so `Deserialize` now returns an `InvalidArgument` error instead of crashing. Serializing early-exit compilations stays as is.

head_commit.message:
PR #52246: [XLA:GPU] Provision and select locality-domain streams at execution

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52246

📝 Summary of Changes

Runs locality-domain regions on dedicated streams at execution time, builds on [#52124](https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52124).

- `Backend`: keeps a `StreamPool` per executor and locality domain, created with `StreamExecutor::CreateStreamInLocalityDomain`.
- `ServiceExecutableRunOptions` exposes a borrower for them, passed by `LocalClient`, `Service` and `HloRunner`.
- `GpuExecutable`: finds the locality domains referenced by its `AsyncStartThunk`s, validates them against the compiled and runtime locality-domain counts, and leases one stream per domain for the execution.
- `Thunk::ExecuteParams`: carries the leased streams in `locality_domain_streams`.
- `AsyncStartThunk`: runs locality-domain regions on the leased stream, replacing the `Unimplemented` placeholder from #51737.
- `CudaStream`: records the green context a stream was created in, and exposes it through `green_context()`.

🎯 Justification

This PR connects the stream building blocks from [#52124](https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52124) to execution, so an XLA program can run selected regions on a specific locality domain.

🚀 Kind of Contribution

✨ New Feature, 🧪 Tests

📊 Benchmark

N/A: this enables locality-domain execution. Annotating computations to run on a domain comes in a follow-up PR.

🧪 Unit Tests

`GpuExecutableLocalityDomainTest`:
- `NoReferencesDoNotInvokeLocalityBorrower`: programs without locality-domain regions never borrow.
- `ReferencedDomainRequiresSupportedCounts`, `NegativeCompileLocalityCountIsRejected`, `RuntimeWithoutLocalityDomainsReportsUnsupported`, `CompileRuntimeCountMismatchRejectsDomainOutsideSmallerCount`: count validation.
- `MissingBorrowerIsRejected`, `OutOfRangeDomainIdIsRejected`, `BorrowerErrorIsPropagatedWithContext`: error paths.
- `NestedDuplicateDomainsDeduplicateAndKeepLeaseAlive`: one lease per domain, held for the whole execution.

Also:
- `GpuExecutableRuntimeTest.LocalityDomainStreamsAreExcludedFromGenericStreamCounts`: locality-domain streams don't inflate the compute and communication stream counts.
- `AsyncThunkTest.LocalityDomainStreamSelection`: the nested thunks run on the stream leased for their domain.

## 🧪 Execution Tests

These run on a single GPU, and skip on GPUs with fewer than two locality domains.

- `GpuExecutableLocalityDomainTest.BackendPoolsSeparateReuseAndInjectGreenContextStreams`: `Backend` pools stay separate per domain and reuse returned streams; regions on two domains execute on streams in different green contexts.
- `AsyncThunkTest.LocalityDomainsExecuteIndependentDefaultMemoryReadsAndSynchronize`: two locality-domain regions read the same buffer and copy it on their own domain's streams; checks the streams used and the results.

display_title: Add GPU executable load micro-benchmarks

head_commit.message:
Add GPU executable load micro-benchmarks

None of our existing GPU benchmarks measures how long it takes to load a serialized executable or how much host memory a loaded executable keeps alive. We want to reduce the host-side cost of loading AOT compiled GPU executables, so we need a baseline first.

This change adds `BM_LoadSerializedExecutable` (PjRt `LoadSerializedExecutable`) and `BM_GpuAotFromSerializedAndLoad` (deserializing the AOT compilation result and loading it into an `Executable`, below the PjRt layer) to `//xla/pjrt/gpu:se_gpu_pjrt_client_benchmark_test`. `BM_HloModuleFromProto` measures only the creation of the optimized `HloModule` from its proto plus its fingerprint, which is an upper bound of what we can save by not materializing the module. `BM_FirstExecuteAfterLoad` and `BM_ExecuteAfterDeserialize` cover the first and the steady state executions after loading. The destruction of the loaded objects is not part of the measured time.

All of them except `BM_ExecuteAfterDeserialize` also report the heap bytes retained by one result (for `BM_FirstExecuteAfterLoad` after the first execution) as a `heap_bytes_retained` counter. This counter is based on `mallinfo`, so it's only reported with glibc.

The benchmarks run on a tiny module, a synthetic chain of 500 dots and two real models from `xla/tools/benchmarks/hlo` (Gemma4 2B and a MaxText train step). The execution benchmarks use zero-initialized arguments and skip the MaxText module since it donates its arguments. The H100 variant now runs on a full GPU since the Gemma4 arguments don't fit into a MIG partition.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1013781571

display_title: Previously, `jax.profiler.TraceAnnotation` and `StepTraceAnnotation` only emitted `TraceMe` events, leaving Nsight Systems (`nsys`) and Nsight Compute (`ncu`) without JAX user or step ranges on the NVTX timeline.

head_commit.message:
Previously, `jax.profiler.TraceAnnotation` and `StepTraceAnnotation` only emitted `TraceMe` events, leaving Nsight Systems (`nsys`) and Nsight Compute (`ncu`) without JAX user or step ranges on the NVTX timeline.

- Update `TraceMeWrapper` in `xla/python/profiler.cc` to format the label (including `kwargs` metadata such as `step_num`), register it in a bounded cache via `tsl::profiler::RegisterString`, and push/pop an NVTX range on `DefaultProfilerDomain()` when NVTX is active, enabling `nsys --capture-range=nvtx` with zero overhead when NVTX is not injected.
- Invoke `cuProfilerStart`/`cuProfilerStop` in `ProfileSession` when an external GPU profiler is attached, allow `log_dir=None` in `start_trace`, and add unit tests in `profiler_test.py`.

display_title: PR #47839: [XLA:GPU] Add cuDNN non-GEMM pointwise fusion support via TensorIR engine

head_commit.message:
PR #47839: [XLA:GPU] Add cuDNN non-GEMM pointwise fusion support via TensorIR engine

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/47839

## Summary

This PR adds support for lowering non-GEMM HLO pointwise fusions to the cuDNN graph API using the `CUDNN_GENERIC_MEMBOUND_FUSION_TENSOR_IR_ENGINE` (cuDNN's dedicated memory-bound TensorIR engine). The feature is controlled by a new flag `--xla_gpu_cudnn_non_gemm_fusion_level`.

### TensorIR engine selection

For non-GEMM (memory-bound) fusions, `PrepareGraph` in `cudnn_fusion_compiler.cc` sets `force_tensor_ir=true` in `EngineOptions`. In `CudnnGraph::Prepare` (`cuda_dnn.cc`), this deselects engines that report `NUMERICAL_NOTE_TENSOR_CORE` (the CUTLASS FALLBACK engines, eng0-eng2), leaving only `CUDNN_GENERIC_MEMBOUND_FUSION_TENSOR_IR_ENGINE` (eng3). GEMM fusions continue to use the full engine set.

### Extended `cudnn_fusion_compiler.cc`

- **Non-GEMM parameter setup**: Added a parameter-binding path for fusions with no gemm/conv adapter, using `DimensionsAndStrides` directly from the HLO shape.
- **Broadcast lowering**: Fixed same-rank and rank-expanding broadcasts. Non-trivial broadcasts are represented via a logical reshape + pointwise identity so cuDNN sees a full-shape virtual tensor.
- **Logical ops**: `kAnd`, `kOr`, `kNot` now map to cuDNN `LOGICAL_{AND,OR,NOT}` for `PRED`-typed operands (bitwise variants remain unsupported).
- **Clamp fix**: Corrected operand ordering to match XLA semantics: `min(max(value, lower), upper)`.
- **Constant handling**: Extended from scalar-only to any single-element constant (e.g. `s32[1]`, `f32[1,1]`). For non-GEMM/conv fusions, constants are always tagged `COMPILE_TIME_CONST`; GEMM/conv fusions keep the prior behavior of runtime scalar tensors for non-scalar-shaped inputs.
- **Compute type for compare**: `kCompare` derives its compute type from the first operand's type (inputs are the arithmetic type; output is `PRED`).
- **Reduce disabled for non-GEMM fusions**: `kReduce` (including rank-preserving reduction lowering) is now rejected with `UnimplementedError` when the fusion has no gemm/conv adapter; reduce support is unchanged for GEMM/conv fusions. Variadic (tuple-shaped) reduce remains unsupported everywhere.

### Autotuner integration

`IsSupportedCudnnFusion` in `xla/backends/gpu/autotuner/cudnn.cc` is extended to accept non-GEMM fusions that aren't already tagged with kCustom when `xla_gpu_cudnn_non_gemm_fusion_level >= 1`, enabling autotuning over cuDNN/Native emitter and other backends for these fusions.

### New flag

```
--xla_gpu_cudnn_non_gemm_fusion_level=<int>
  0: Disabled (default)
  1: Compile pointwise fusions with cuDNN
```

### Tests

`xla/backends/gpu/codegen/cudnn_test.cc` has broad coverage including: pointwise elementwise ops, broadcasts, logical ops, clamp, reciprocal (`f32`), concat, slice, reshape/bitcast, and various dtype combinations, with test names/traits reorganized and shapes reduced to keep runtime down. `cudnn_non_gemm_fusion_rewriter_test.cc` covers the rewriter pass itself, including the multi-concatenate skip case.

display_title: [XLA] Simplify the identity map in ComputeEpilogueInputToOutputIndexing.

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Simplify the identity map in ComputeEpilogueInputToOutputIndexing.

`ComputeEpilogueInputToOutputIndexing` only ran `Simplify()` while walking a
non-trivial hero->root use chain. When the root *is* the hero, the raw
identity map was returned instead. With size-1 dimensions the two forms
differ structurally (`(d0, d1, d2) -> (0, d1, d2)` vs.
`(d0, d1, d2) -> (d0, d1, d2)`) even though they are semantically equal, so
`IndexingMap::operator==` reports them as different.

The multi-output concatenate emitter compares the epilogue indexing of all
roots and fails with

```
RET_CHECK failure (xla/codegen/emitters/concatenate_kernel_emitter.cc:200)
UseConcatenateFusion should have ensured all roots share the same epilogue indexing
```

for a fusion where one root is `divide(concatenate(...), ...)` and the other
root is a bare `concatenate`, as soon as the shapes contain a size-1
dimension.

Simplify the initial identity map so the result is canonical regardless of
the chain length. Adds a unit test for the indexing analysis and a GPU
emitter lit test with the failing fusion.

Fixes https://github.com/EnzymeAD/Reactant.jl/issues/3681

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1013012065

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Accept float-normalized add combiners in Triton scans and share the check with CanTritonHandleScan.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Accept float-normalized add combiners in Triton scans and share the check with CanTritonHandleScan.

Add `IsAdditiveScanCombiner`. It requires a combiner with two parameters of the output element type whose root is `tuple(x, x)`, where `x` is `add(p0, p1)` or `convert(add(convert(p0), convert(p1)))`. Use it in:

- `EmitScan`, which now accepts the `convert` form. This fixes `bf16` scans on pre-Hopper GPUs (e.g. A100, A6000), where `GpuFloatSupport` normalizes `bf16` `kAdd` and `FloatNormalization` wraps it in `kConvert`s. `EmitScan` now also rejects combiners whose carry differs from the output, because the lowering derives the carry from the output, and combiners whose add operands are not the parameters.
- `CanTritonHandleScan`, which accepted any associative combiner supported by Triton, so `ScanRewriterTriton` could create scan fusions that `EmitScan` rejects (e.g. a max scan). `FusionBlockLevelRewriter` checks the fusion after `FloatNormalization`, so `CanTritonHandleScan` must accept the `convert` form as well.

Make the combiners in `ScanSupportTest` valid `tuple(add, add)` roots, and check the forbid reason in each negative test. Add support tests for non-additive combiners, a device test for the `convert` form, and a lit test that compiles a `bf16` cumulative sum to a Triton scan kernel.

display_title: [XLA] Simplify the identity map in ComputeEpilogueInputToOutputIndexing.

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Simplify the identity map in ComputeEpilogueInputToOutputIndexing.

`ComputeEpilogueInputToOutputIndexing` only ran `Simplify()` while walking a
non-trivial hero->root use chain. When the root *is* the hero, the raw
identity map was returned instead. With size-1 dimensions the two forms
differ structurally (`(d0, d1, d2) -> (0, d1, d2)` vs.
`(d0, d1, d2) -> (d0, d1, d2)`) even though they are semantically equal, so
`IndexingMap::operator==` reports them as different.

The multi-output concatenate emitter compares the epilogue indexing of all
roots and fails with

```
RET_CHECK failure (xla/codegen/emitters/concatenate_kernel_emitter.cc:200)
UseConcatenateFusion should have ensured all roots share the same epilogue indexing
```

for a fusion where one root is `divide(concatenate(...), ...)` and the other
root is a bare `concatenate`, as soon as the shapes contain a size-1
dimension.

Simplify the initial identity map so the result is canonical regardless of
the chain length. Adds a unit test for the indexing analysis and a GPU
emitter lit test with the failing fusion.

Fixes https://github.com/EnzymeAD/Reactant.jl/issues/3681

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Remove disabled autotune backends when no backend list is set.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Remove disabled autotune backends when no backend list is set.

`ConfigAssignerPass::GetEnabledBackends` removes disabled backends from `xla_gpu_experimental_autotune_backends` and passes the result on as an allowlist, where an empty list means all backends. DebugOptions that don't start from `DefaultDebugOptionsIgnoringFlags()`, e.g. ones serialized before it populated the list, can leave the list empty. Then nothing is removed, and disabled backends stay enabled, e.g. `TENSOR_IR` without `xla_gpu_experimental_enable_tensor_ir`.

Populate an empty list with all backends, like the defaults do, before removing the disabled ones. All existing rules (binary libraries, emitters, Triton, TensorIR) then apply to an empty list too.

display_title: Use Executable accessors in HloRunnerLegacy

head_commit.message:
Use Executable accessors in HloRunnerLegacy

HloRunnerLegacy read the input/output alias config and the debug options from `Executable::module()`, which doesn't work for executables that were compiled without an embedded HloModule (`embed_hlo_module=false`) or that will be loaded without one in the future.

So this change reads the alias config through `Executable::input_output_alias_config()`, only updates the entry computation layout if the executable has a module, and falls back to the debug options from the flags if there is no module. Nothing changes for executables that have a module.

The new test runs a GPU executable compiled with `embed_hlo_module=false` through HloRunnerLegacy.

display_title: Add module metadata accessors to Executable

head_commit.message:
Add module metadata accessors to Executable

Callers that need the input/output aliasing, the buffer donors, the static device assignment or the entry computation layout of an executable currently read them from the HloModule. That doesn't work for GPU executables that don't keep the module (`embed_hlo_module=false`, and soon loaded AOT executables).

So this change adds `input_output_alias_config()`, `buffer_donor_config()`, `static_device_assignment()` and `entry_computation_layout()` to `Executable`. By default they read from the module, so nothing changes for other backends. `GpuExecutable` overrides them and stores the values at creation time. The aliasing is rebuilt from the output info that is already part of `GpuExecutableProto`. The other values come from the module, the serialized module config, or (with `embed_hlo_module=false`) from the compiler via `GpuExecutable::Params`. The compiler now also passes the partition size that way, so `GpuExecutable::partition_size()` is correct without the module.

This way callers can be migrated to the new accessors in follow-up changes without needing the module.

display_title: Don't require an HloModule for RunAsync VLOGs

head_commit.message:
Don't require an HloModule for RunAsync VLOGs

PjRtStreamExecutorRawLoadedExecutable::Execute logs the module name before and after RunAsync via `Executable::module()`, which CHECK-fails when the executable doesn't hold an HloModule. So turning on `VLOG(1)` crashes the GPU execute path for such executables.

This change uses `Executable::name()` instead, which the neighbouring `VLOG(2)` statements already use. GpuExecutable overrides it to return the module name it stores itself, so the log shows the real name even without a module. (Only the base class default falls back to a placeholder.)

display_title: Reject deserialization of early-exit GPU executables

head_commit.message:
Reject deserialization of early-exit GPU executables

For executables compiled with `xla_early_exit_with_layouts`, `StreamExecutorExecutable::SerializeExecutable` only writes the compile options. `StreamExecutorExecutable::Deserialize` turned that back into an executable without a `CompiledModule`, which hits the `CHECK` in the constructor that requires an `HloModule`. So loading such a serialized executable crashed the process.

Loading early-exit executables isn't supported anyway (`CommonPjRtClient::LoadInternal` rejects them), so `Deserialize` now returns an `InvalidArgument` error instead of crashing. Serializing early-exit compilations stays as is.

display_title: Add GPU executable load micro-benchmarks

head_commit.message:
Add GPU executable load micro-benchmarks

None of our existing GPU benchmarks measures how long it takes to load a serialized executable or how much host memory a loaded executable keeps alive. We want to reduce the host-side cost of loading AOT compiled GPU executables, so we need a baseline first.

This change adds `BM_LoadSerializedExecutable` (PjRt `LoadSerializedExecutable`) and `BM_GpuAotFromSerializedAndLoad` (deserializing the AOT compilation result and loading it into an `Executable`, below the PjRt layer) to `//xla/pjrt/gpu:se_gpu_pjrt_client_benchmark_test`. `BM_HloModuleFromProto` measures only the creation of the optimized `HloModule` from its proto plus its fingerprint, which is an upper bound of what we can save by not materializing the module. `BM_FirstExecuteAfterLoad` and `BM_ExecuteAfterDeserialize` cover the first and the steady state executions after loading. The destruction of the loaded objects is not part of the measured time.

All of them except `BM_ExecuteAfterDeserialize` also report the heap bytes retained by one result (for `BM_FirstExecuteAfterLoad` after the first execution) as a `heap_bytes_retained` counter. This counter is based on `mallinfo`, so it's only reported with glibc.

The benchmarks run on a tiny module, a synthetic chain of 500 dots and two real models from `xla/tools/benchmarks/hlo` (Gemma4 2B and a MaxText train step). The execution benchmarks use zero-initialized arguments and skip the MaxText module since it donates its arguments. The H100 variant now runs on a full GPU since the Gemma4 arguments don't fit into a MIG partition.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1010369592

With `--xla_gpu_generate_line_info` (or `--xla_gpu_generate_debug_info`), ptxas is asked to keep line info, but kernels from the MLIR emitters had no `.loc` directives, so Nsight Compute could not map SASS back to source.

display_title: PR #47839: [XLA:GPU] Add cuDNN non-GEMM pointwise fusion support via TensorIR engine

head_commit.message:
PR #47839: [XLA:GPU] Add cuDNN non-GEMM pointwise fusion support via TensorIR engine

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/47839

## Summary

This PR adds support for lowering non-GEMM HLO pointwise fusions to the cuDNN graph API using the `CUDNN_GENERIC_MEMBOUND_FUSION_TENSOR_IR_ENGINE` (cuDNN's dedicated memory-bound TensorIR engine). The feature is controlled by a new flag `--xla_gpu_cudnn_non_gemm_fusion_level`.

### TensorIR engine selection

For non-GEMM (memory-bound) fusions, `PrepareGraph` in `cudnn_fusion_compiler.cc` sets `force_tensor_ir=true` in `EngineOptions`. In `CudnnGraph::Prepare` (`cuda_dnn.cc`), this deselects engines that report `NUMERICAL_NOTE_TENSOR_CORE` (the CUTLASS FALLBACK engines, eng0-eng2), leaving only `CUDNN_GENERIC_MEMBOUND_FUSION_TENSOR_IR_ENGINE` (eng3). GEMM fusions continue to use the full engine set.

### Extended `cudnn_fusion_compiler.cc`

- **Non-GEMM parameter setup**: Added a parameter-binding path for fusions with no gemm/conv adapter, using `DimensionsAndStrides` directly from the HLO shape.
- **Broadcast lowering**: Fixed same-rank and rank-expanding broadcasts. Non-trivial broadcasts are represented via a logical reshape + pointwise identity so cuDNN sees a full-shape virtual tensor.
- **Logical ops**: `kAnd`, `kOr`, `kNot` now map to cuDNN `LOGICAL_{AND,OR,NOT}` for `PRED`-typed operands (bitwise variants remain unsupported).
- **Clamp fix**: Corrected operand ordering to match XLA semantics: `min(max(value, lower), upper)`.
- **Constant handling**: Extended from scalar-only to any single-element constant (e.g. `s32[1]`, `f32[1,1]`). For non-GEMM/conv fusions, constants are always tagged `COMPILE_TIME_CONST`; GEMM/conv fusions keep the prior behavior of runtime scalar tensors for non-scalar-shaped inputs.
- **Compute type for compare**: `kCompare` derives its compute type from the first operand's type (inputs are the arithmetic type; output is `PRED`).
- **Reduce disabled for non-GEMM fusions**: `kReduce` (including rank-preserving reduction lowering) is now rejected with `UnimplementedError` when the fusion has no gemm/conv adapter; reduce support is unchanged for GEMM/conv fusions. Variadic (tuple-shaped) reduce remains unsupported everywhere.

### Autotuner integration

`IsSupportedCudnnFusion` in `xla/backends/gpu/autotuner/cudnn.cc` is extended to accept non-GEMM fusions that aren't already tagged with kCustom when `xla_gpu_cudnn_non_gemm_fusion_level >= 1`, enabling autotuning over cuDNN/Native emitter and other backends for these fusions.

### New flag

```
--xla_gpu_cudnn_non_gemm_fusion_level=<int>
  0: Disabled (default)
  1: Compile pointwise fusions with cuDNN
```

### Tests

`xla/backends/gpu/codegen/cudnn_test.cc` has broad coverage including: pointwise elementwise ops, broadcasts, logical ops, clamp, reciprocal (`f32`), concat, slice, reshape/bitcast, and various dtype combinations, with test names/traits reorganized and shapes reduced to keep runtime down. `cudnn_non_gemm_fusion_rewriter_test.cc` covers the rewriter pass itself, including the multi-concatenate skip case.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Fix use-after-free from orphaned async kernel compilation futures

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Fix use-after-free from orphaned async kernel compilation futures

Asynchronous kernel compilation tasks scheduled via `KernelCompiler` capture
`IrEmitterContext*` and `BufferAssignment*` (owned by `CompileModuleToLlvmIr`)
as well as `CubinCustomKernelCompiler*`. Returning early on an error before
awaiting all launched futures allows worker threads on the compilation thread
pool to dereference these objects after they have been destroyed.

Fix three error paths that could orphan in-flight compilation futures:
- In `CompileModuleToLlvmIr`, await both `future_thunks` and
  `future_constants_binary` before propagating any error from either future.
- In `ThunkEmitter::EmitConditional`, resolve the predicate allocation slice
  before launching `EmitHloComputation` futures for the branch computations.
- In `EmitBitonicSort`, return a `Future<std::unique_ptr<Thunk>>` from
  `emit_thunk` and collect all futures into `thunks` so `tsl::JoinFutures`
  always awaits previously launched bitonic sort kernels even if a later stage
  fails.

head_commit.message:
PR #52290: [ROCm][IFRT IR] Accept the ROCm platform in IFRT IR compilation passes

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52290

📝 Summary of Changes

`IfrtVerifyDeviceTypeConsistencyPass` and `IfrtPrecompileAtomProgramPreprocessingPass`
recognize only the TPU, CUDA and CPU platforms (plus `host` in the verifier). So
compiling an IFRT IR program whose atom programs run on ROCm devices fails:
- `IfrtVerifyDeviceTypeConsistencyPass::initialize` logs `Unsupported platform: rocm`
  and fails.
- `IfrtPrecompileAtomProgramPreprocessingPass` reports
  `'ifrt.Call' op Unsupported platform for call op: rocm`.
`BasicAtomProgramCompiler` already accepts `rocm`, so these two passes were the only
blockers. This change accepts `xla::RocmName()` wherever `xla::CudaName()` is accepted.

🎯 Justification

Found while compiling Shardy MPMD programs (lowered with `jaxlib._sdy_mpmd.lower_to_ifrt`)
with `IfrtIrProgramCompiler` on the ROCm PJRT plugin.

🚀 Kind of Contribution
Please remove what does not apply:
✨ New Feature,

📊 Benchmark (for Performance Improvements)
Please measure and include speedups for one of the public HLOs in
`compiler/xla/tools/benchmarks/hlo/`.

🧪 Unit Tests:
- New `ifrt_verify_device_type_consistency_rocm.mlir`: an all-ROCm call passes, and a
  call spanning ROCm and CPU devices reports the single-platform error. It is a
  separate file because the existing test's RUN line fixes the device-to-platform
  mapping, which its out-of-range device case depends on.
- New RUN line in `ifrt_precompile_atom_program_preprocessing.mlir` with
  `platform_names=rocm,rocm`, reusing the existing Shardy checks.
    bazel test //xla/python/ifrt/ir/compilation/tests:ifrt_verify_device_type_consistency_rocm.mlir.test \
      //xla/python/ifrt/ir/compilation/tests:ifrt_verify_device_type_consistency.mlir.test \
      //xla/python/ifrt/ir/compilation/tests:ifrt_precompile_atom_program_preprocessing.mlir.test
All three pass. With the two pass changes reverted, both new ROCm cases fail with the
errors above.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Reland: Scale intermediate tile sizes by byte width in EstimateNumWarps.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Reland: Scale intermediate tile sizes by byte width in EstimateNumWarps.

`EstimateNumWarps` picks the warp count from the largest padded tile in the fusion. Broadcasts, `iota` and narrow intermediates such as `pred` comparisons feeding a reduction inflate that size by 4x or more, which selects 4-8 warps where 2-4 are faster.

Keep counting operand and root tiles in full, but ignore non-root `broadcast` and `constant` tiles, size non-root `iota` by its extent along `iota_dimension`, and scale other non-root array tiles by `min(element_bytes, 4) / 4`. `EstimateNumWarps` now takes the `HloFusionAdaptor` to tell fusion operands from intermediates.

This relands cl/1008957649 (rolled back in cl/1010131399) without its `blocks_per_core` change to the compute-time estimate. That change regressed an inference benchmark by 1.5-1.66x.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Disable buffer sharing for phased block-cluster fusions.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Disable buffer sharing for phased block-cluster fusions.

`PhasedBlockClusterFusion` (cl/1013683054) executes multiple nested fusions sequentially inside a single Hopper thread-block-cluster kernel. Without an explicit `GpuAliasInfo` rule, `BufferAssigner` falls back to `FusionCanShareBufferHint` and may reuse a shared outer operand's buffer for an earlier phase's output slice, either failing slice-aliasing checks or overwriting input data still needed by a later phase.

Return `false` from `GpuAliasInfo::MayAlias` for `__phased_block_cluster` fusions so phase outputs are allocated in buffers disjoint from outer operands, and enable execution coverage for shared outer operands across phases.

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/51671

📝 Summary of Changes
Run GPU constant-name sanitization across all HLO execution threads instead of only the main execution thread.

This ensures constants inside async computations created by explicit stream annotations are sanitized before GPU code generation. A regression test was added for a constant inside a stream-annotated call.

display_title: Build the HloModule for profiling only when needed in GpuExecutable

head_commit.message:
Build the HloModule for profiling only when needed in GpuExecutable

A GpuExecutable that only keeps the serialized HloModule (see `GetOrCreateHloModule`) has no module for two profiler features: the per-instruction trace annotations and the debug info that XlaDebugInfoManager hands out at the end of a trace. Building the module at construction time just for that would defeat the point of not keeping it around.

So this change builds the module on the first execution that sees an active profiler (through the new `MaybePrepareProfiling`). That execution and all later ones use the full annotations prepared from the module instead of the name-only ones, and the module gets registered with XlaDebugInfoManager like any other module. (If the module was already built for another reason, we use that one.) Without a profiler nothing changes, so the module is never built. If building the module fails, we log a warning once and keep using the name-only annotations.

Executables that have an HloModule behave exactly as before.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1012088899

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Wait on the host for cross-device events before enqueuing D2D copies.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Wait on the host for cross-device events before enqueuing D2D copies.

A D2D copy from GPU 0 to GPU 1 makes GPU 0's stream wait for an event on GPU 1.
If that event is stuck behind a collective on GPU 1 and a context-synchronizing
call (like cuModuleLoad) runs on GPU 0, GPU 0 can never launch its half of the collective, which creates a deadlock.

Waiting for the event asynchronously on the host instead keeps GPU 0's stream free, so GPU 0 can still launch its half of the collective.

The new behavior is off by default and behind `XLA_PJRT_GPU_HOST_WAIT_CROSS_DEVICE_COPIES=true`.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1010481212

name: CI ROCm
display_title: Build the HloModule of a GpuExecutable on demand

head_commit.message:
Build the HloModule of a GpuExecutable on demand

We want to stop building the `HloModule` when we load a `GpuExecutable` from
its serialized form, because the executable doesn't need it to run. But some
code (profiling, debugging) still needs the module, so it has to be built on
demand.

So this change replaces `GpuExecutable::Params::debug_module` with
`Params::hlo_module`, a variant that holds either nothing, the module, or the
serialized module (`HloModuleProtoWithConfig`). With a serialized module the
executable passes a factory to the new `Executable` constructor, and
`Executable::GetOrCreateHloModule` builds the module with it the first time
someone needs it. After that `has_module()` returns true. The built module gets
the `pjrt_id` of the serialized module as its unique id, so profiler
annotations and debug info refer to the same id before and after the module is
built. Therefore `Create` rejects a serialized module without a non-negative
`pjrt_id`.

Building the module is observable on purpose, so that we can find the code
that still needs it: It's logged with the reason (and with a stack trace at
`VLOG(1)`), it increments the new counter
`/xla/gpu/hlo_module_materializations{reason}`, and the new flag
`--xla_gpu_experimental_fail_on_lazy_hlo_module_materialization` turns it into
a `FailedPrecondition` error (if it's set at compile time or at load time).

Only modules that are there at construction are registered with the
`XlaDebugInfoManager`, so the destructor now remembers whether it has to
unregister the module instead of looking at `has_module()`. And `ToProto` now
looks at the module only once, so that the serialized module and constants are
consistent even if the module gets built concurrently. If the module hasn't been
built yet, `ToProto` writes the serialized module, which the executable shares
with the factory.

Serialized executables don't carry a `pjrt_id`. So once `FromProto` passes the
serialized module instead of building it, it has to assign a fresh id first. I
left a TODO for that in `FromProto`.

Nothing creates executables with a serialized module yet (`FromProto` still
builds the module), so this doesn't change any behaviour.

The tests are in the new CPU-only target
`//xla/service/gpu:gpu_executable_hlo_module_test` so that the concurrency
test can also run with TSAN.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1012082361

unregister the module instead of looking at `has_module()`. And `ToProto` now
looks at the module only once, so that the serialized module and constants are
consistent even if the module gets built concurrently. If the module hasn't been
built yet, `ToProto` writes the serialized module, which the executable shares
with the factory.

Serialized executables don't carry a `pjrt_id`. So once `FromProto` passes the
serialized module instead of building it, it has to assign a fresh id first. I
left a TODO for that in `FromProto`.

Nothing creates executables with a serialized module yet (`FromProto` still
builds the module), so this doesn't change any behaviour.

The tests are in the new CPU-only target
`//xla/service/gpu:gpu_executable_hlo_module_test` so that the concurrency
test can also run with TSAN.

head_commit.message:
PR #52257: [ROCm profiler] Keep each kernel's own kernel_details in a graph launch

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52257

## Problem

when running through command buffers (HIP graphs), one `hipGraphLaunch` yields one HIP API record and one dispatch record per graph node, all under one correlation id. In the trace, every kernel of that launch shows the same `kernel_details`: the registers, shared memory, grid and block of whichever dispatch record reached the buffer first. That first kernel's row is correct, however, the rest kernels' details are incorrect.

📝 Summary of Changes

- Remove both copies. `KernelEvent` already fills each activity row from its own dispatch record, and `kernel_details` is exported only for activity kernel rows. The host row still takes `device_id` and `stream_id` from the first record.
- Remove the activity-side `memset_info` copy. The API row never carries it, and the tracer emits no Memset activities today.
- `MultipleActivitiesPerCorrelationIdAllExported` now gives its three kernels distinct grids and checks that each exported row keeps its own grid. On the old code, kernel_b and kernel_c show kernel_a's `grid:4,1,1`.

`rocm_collector_test` and `rocm_tracer_test_amdgpu_any` pass locally and under `--config=rocm_ci_hermetic` on MI355X.

🎯 Justification

| Measure | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| HIP graph of 3 fixed-shape kernels, 5 launches per run: rows whose details differ from their own launch | 10 of 15, in 3 of 3 runs | 0, in 6 of 6 runs |
| JAX step with `--xla_gpu_autotune_level=0`, 5 graph launches of 3 kernels: distinct `kernel_details` per launch | 1, in 3 of 3 runs | 3, in 3 of 3 runs |
| MaxText llama2-7b training, 8 GPUs: graph kernels with one `regs`/`static_shared` across all their rows | 14 of 142 (1 run) | 142 of 142 (2 runs) |
| Same run: graph kernels that also launch outside a graph and match those launches | 0 of 8 | 8 of 8 |
| Blit kernel grid / block | `0,0,0 / 0,0,0` | `1,1,1 / 512,1,1` |

🚀 Kind of Contribution
Please remove what does not apply: 🐛 Bug Fix

Copybara import of the project:

--
99c67a6473b1ffc52b4f3224a4846428e4cf0459 by cj401-amd <chunyjin@amd.com>:

[ROCm profiler] Keep each kernel's own kernel_details in a graph launch

One hipGraphLaunch yields many kernel-dispatch records under one correlation
id. ApiActivityInfoExchange copied the kernel_info of the first record to
arrive onto the HIP API row, then copied that back onto every activity kernel
row with the same correlation id. So every kernel in a graph launch showed the
registers, shared memory, grid and block of whichever record reached the
buffer first.

Two more cases went through the same copy. kernel_info and memcpy_info share a
union, so when a memcpy record arrived first, every kernel row showed the
copy's bytes read as kernel details. And a copy API served by a blit kernel
gave that kernel a zero grid and block, because the API row only received the
first 16 bytes of the kernel's details.

KernelEvent already fills each activity row's kernel_info from its own
dispatch record and code-object symbol, and kernel_details is exported only
for activity kernel rows, so the activity loop no longer overwrites it. The
API loop no longer copies kernel_info onto the HIP API row either: that row
does not export it, and the first record may not be a kernel, in which case
the copy read a memcpy's bytes as KernelDetails. The host row still takes
device_id and stream_id from the first record. The activity loop's Memset case
no longer copies memset_info from the API row, which never carries it; the
tracer emits no Memset activities today, so this changes nothing yet.

MultipleActivitiesPerCorrelationIdAllExported now gives its three kernels
distinct grids and checks that each exported row keeps its own.
TestAddKernelEventAndExport now initialises its activity's kernel_info,
which it used to export uninitialised. Both exchange tests stop setting
kernel details on the HIP API event: those never reached the output, and the
API row now carries none.

Merging this change closes #52257

name: CI ROCm
display_title: Enable remote_download_minimal on JAX Windows CPU CI

head_commit.message:
Enable remote_download_minimal on JAX Windows CPU CI

`JAX_WINDOWS_X86_CPU_GITHUB_ACTIONS` in `xla/build_tools/ci/build.py` runs `bazel build` with remote execution on RBE to verify that CPU `jaxlib` and the JAX CPU test targets build on Windows without executing tests on the runner. Unlike the Linux JAX CI builds (`JAX_LINUX_X86_CPU_BZLMOD_GITHUB_ACTIONS` and `JAX_LINUX_X86_GPU_T4_GITHUB_ACTIONS`), it did not pass `--remote_download_minimal`, causing Bazel to download ~17,000 cached C++ object files and libraries to the Windows runner on every PR.

Therefore this change enables `remote_download_minimal=True` on `JAX_WINDOWS_X86_CPU_GITHUB_ACTIONS`. On GitHub Actions (`openxla/xla#52218`), this reduces the `JAX Windows x86 CPU` job duration from **38m 55s** to **12m 32s** (`607s` in `Run build.py`, saving **26m 23s** per PR).

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1013709778

modules succeeds when constant literals were dropped.

- `//xla/pjrt/c_api_client:pjrt_c_api_client_test`: verifies GetHloModules on an

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Add PhasedBlockClusterFusion emitter.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Add PhasedBlockClusterFusion emitter.

Dependent small fusions are often dominated by fixed kernel launch and scheduling overheads when run as separate kernels. Executing dependent fusions as sequential phases of a single Hopper (SM90+) thread-block-cluster kernel separated by cluster barriers pays that launch overhead only once while exchanging intermediate results via DRAM or caches. Note that `ThreadBlockSpecializedFusion` (cl/1012181303) combines independent fusions across disjoint CTAs and is complementary.

Current limitations (to be lifted in follow-up CLs):

* Only straight-line chains of `kLoop` fusions
* Nested fusion must fit a single thread block cluster
* No buffer aliasing with fusion outputs

display_title: Ignore element size and memory space in CommonPjRtClient::Delinearize.

head_commit.message:
Ignore element size and memory space in CommonPjRtClient::Delinearize.

XLA `Literal` shapes always clear `element_size_in_bits` to 0 (storing sub-byte elements unpacked at 1 byte per element) and use the default `memory_space`, whereas PJRT buffer shapes carry packed `element_size_in_bits` (for example, 4 for `S4`/`U4` or 2 for `S2`/`U2`) and the buffer's `memory_space` (such as `Layout::kHostMemorySpace`). Comparing `literal_layout != shape.layout()` in `CommonPjRtClient::Delinearize` therefore always evaluated `need_transpose = true` for every sub-byte buffer and every host-memory-space buffer, even when the rest of the layout already matched. For sub-byte transfers, that forced an unnecessary heap allocation and zero-fill of `staged_buffer` at the full unpacked byte size followed by an identity `TransposePlan::Execute` copy on top of `UnpackIntN`, leaving the direct `UnpackIntN` branch unreachable.

Compare layouts in `CommonPjRtClient::Delinearize` with `Layout::Equal().IgnoreElementSize().IgnoreMemorySpace()`, taking the direct unpack or `memcpy` fast path when layouts otherwise match (and guarding `std::memcpy` on 0-byte outputs). On `BM_DelinearizeInt4`, this speeds up `S4` delinearization by 3.1x–3.7x for cache-resident buffers (4 Ki and 1 Mi elements, reaching 31–37 GiB/s) and by 9.7x for 64 Mi-element buffers (48.1 ms to 4.95 ms) by avoiding transient 64 MiB `staged_buffer` page faults and copies.

Tested with unit tests in `//xla/pjrt:common_pjrt_client_test` covering matching default and non-default `minor_to_major` sub-byte layouts, odd-element tail-byte masking, transposed sub-byte layouts, `kHostMemorySpace` buffers (including 0-element spans), and end-to-end `BufferFromHostLiteral` to `ToLiteral` round-trips, alongside `BM_DelinearizeInt4` microbenchmarks.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: Build the HloModule for profiling only when needed in GpuExecutable

head_commit.message:
Build the HloModule for profiling only when needed in GpuExecutable

A GpuExecutable that only keeps the serialized HloModule (see `GetOrCreateHloModule`) has no module for two profiler features: the per-instruction trace annotations and the debug info that XlaDebugInfoManager hands out at the end of a trace. Building the module at construction time just for that would defeat the point of not keeping it around.

So this change builds the module on the first execution that sees an active profiler (through the new `MaybePrepareProfiling`). That execution and all later ones use the full annotations prepared from the module instead of the name-only ones, and the module gets registered with XlaDebugInfoManager like any other module. (If the module was already built for another reason, we use that one.) Without a profiler nothing changes, so the module is never built. If building the module fails, we log a warning once and keep using the name-only annotations.

Executables that have an HloModule behave exactly as before.

head_commit.message:
PR #51671: XLA:GPU: Sanitize constants on all execution threads

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/51671

📝 Summary of Changes
Run GPU constant-name sanitization across all HLO execution threads instead of only the main execution thread.

This ensures constants inside async computations created by explicit stream annotations are sanitized before GPU code generation. A regression test was added for a constant inside a stream-annotated call.

🎯 Justification
`ExplicitStreamAnnotationAsyncWrapper` creates async computations on the parallel execution thread, while `SanitizeConstantNames` previously ran only on the main execution thread.

As a result, constants in these async computations could reach GPU code generation with unsanitized names and trigger the ConstantNameToGlobalName DCHECK.

This change runs constant-name sanitization across all execution threads while keeping the remaining post-scheduling passes scoped to the main execution thread.

Fixes #50829

🚀 Kind of Contribution
Please remove what does not apply: 🐛 Bug Fix

📊 Benchmark (for Performance Improvements)
NA

🧪 Unit Tests:
Added `GpuCompilerTest.SanitizesConstantNamesInParallelExecutionThread`, which compiles an HLO containing a constant inside a stream-annotated call through the GPU compiler pipeline.

🧪 Execution Tests:
No execution tests added.

[ROCm] [CUDA] Skip re-recording unchanged collectives in command buffers

  re-records every command buffer that holds a collective on every
  execution, so that all participants record their collectives together.
- New flag --xla_gpu_command_buffer_skip_unchanged_collectives (default
  off): when every participant is in this process, the participants agree
  through a host rendezvous and record again only if one of them has to:
  not warmed up, not recorded yet, profiling, or a buffer of these
  collectives moved. The flag is a field of CommandBufferThunkOptions.

display_title: Enable remote_download_minimal on JAX Windows CPU CI

head_commit.message:
Enable remote_download_minimal on JAX Windows CPU CI

`JAX_WINDOWS_X86_CPU_GITHUB_ACTIONS` in `xla/build_tools/ci/build.py` runs `bazel build` with remote execution on RBE to verify that CPU `jaxlib` and the JAX CPU test targets build on Windows without executing tests on the runner. Unlike the Linux JAX CI builds (`JAX_LINUX_X86_CPU_BZLMOD_GITHUB_ACTIONS` and `JAX_LINUX_X86_GPU_T4_GITHUB_ACTIONS`), it did not pass `--remote_download_minimal`, causing Bazel to download ~17,000 cached C++ object files and libraries to the Windows runner on every PR.

Therefore this change enables `remote_download_minimal=True` on `JAX_WINDOWS_X86_CPU_GITHUB_ACTIONS`. On GitHub Actions (`openxla/xla#52218`), this reduces the `JAX Windows x86 CPU` job duration from **38m 55s** to **12m 32s** (`607s` in `Run build.py`, saving **26m 23s** per PR).

display_title: Persist fingerprint and collective resource flag

head_commit.message:
Persist fingerprint and collective resource flag

A deserialized GpuExecutable still needs the HLO module to compute the module fingerprint and to decide whether collectives should use minimal GPU resources. Both are pure functions of the optimized module, so we can compute them at compile time and store them in `GpuExecutableProto` (xla/service/gpu/gpu_executable.proto) instead.

This change adds the `fingerprint` and `collective_use_minimal_resource` fields, writes them in `ToProto` and uses them in `FromProto`. `GpuExecutable::Create` computes the fingerprint from the module unless it's passed in, which happens when deserializing and when the compiler doesn't embed the module. Executables serialized before these fields existed fall back to computing the values from the HLO module, which is still deserialized eagerly for now. Executables without an HLO module have an empty fingerprint and always write `collective_use_minimal_resource=false`, which is the value they used before. If `Params::hlo_module` only holds the serialized module (nothing does that yet), `Create` requires `collective_use_minimal_resource` to be set, because we don't want to build the module just for that and silently using false could differ from what the module would give.

Computing the fingerprint eagerly costs 0.1-0.45% of the JIT compile time (measured on H100 for gemma4_2b, maxtext and a chain of 500 dots, with and without autotuning). That's cheap enough to not justify a lazily computed and cached value.

The fingerprint stored at compile time matches the fingerprint of the module after a serialization round trip (which is what PjRt computed for deserialized executables so far). A new PjRt test checks that for a few non-trivial programs, and I also verified it for all GPU AOT goldens.

The AOT golden comparison ignores both fields since they are derived from the HLO module, which is already ignored.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1012067440

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Add PhasedBlockClusterFusion emitter.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Add PhasedBlockClusterFusion emitter.

Dependent small fusions are often dominated by fixed kernel launch and scheduling overheads when run as separate kernels. Executing dependent fusions as sequential phases of a single Hopper (SM90+) thread-block-cluster kernel separated by cluster barriers pays that launch overhead only once while exchanging intermediate results via DRAM or caches. Note that `ThreadBlockSpecializedFusion` (cl/1012181303) combines independent fusions across disjoint CTAs and is complementary.

Current limitations (to be lifted in follow-up CLs):

* Only straight-line chains of `kLoop` fusions
* Nested fusion must fit a single thread block cluster
* No buffer aliasing with fusion outputs

display_title: PR #47839: [XLA:GPU] Add cuDNN non-GEMM pointwise fusion support via TensorIR engine

head_commit.message:
PR #47839: [XLA:GPU] Add cuDNN non-GEMM pointwise fusion support via TensorIR engine

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/47839

## Summary

This PR adds support for lowering non-GEMM HLO pointwise fusions to the cuDNN graph API using the `CUDNN_GENERIC_MEMBOUND_FUSION_TENSOR_IR_ENGINE` (cuDNN's dedicated memory-bound TensorIR engine). The feature is controlled by a new flag `--xla_gpu_cudnn_non_gemm_fusion_level`.

### TensorIR engine selection

For non-GEMM (memory-bound) fusions, `PrepareGraph` in `cudnn_fusion_compiler.cc` sets `force_tensor_ir=true` in `EngineOptions`. In `CudnnGraph::Prepare` (`cuda_dnn.cc`), this deselects engines that report `NUMERICAL_NOTE_TENSOR_CORE` (the CUTLASS FALLBACK engines, eng0-eng2), leaving only `CUDNN_GENERIC_MEMBOUND_FUSION_TENSOR_IR_ENGINE` (eng3). GEMM fusions continue to use the full engine set.

### Extended `cudnn_fusion_compiler.cc`

- **Non-GEMM parameter setup**: Added a parameter-binding path for fusions with no gemm/conv adapter, using `DimensionsAndStrides` directly from the HLO shape.
- **Broadcast lowering**: Fixed same-rank and rank-expanding broadcasts. Non-trivial broadcasts are represented via a logical reshape + pointwise identity so cuDNN sees a full-shape virtual tensor.
- **Logical ops**: `kAnd`, `kOr`, `kNot` now map to cuDNN `LOGICAL_{AND,OR,NOT}` for `PRED`-typed operands (bitwise variants remain unsupported).
- **Clamp fix**: Corrected operand ordering to match XLA semantics: `min(max(value, lower), upper)`.
- **Constant handling**: Extended from scalar-only to any single-element constant (e.g. `s32[1]`, `f32[1,1]`). For non-GEMM/conv fusions, constants are always tagged `COMPILE_TIME_CONST`; GEMM/conv fusions keep the prior behavior of runtime scalar tensors for non-scalar-shaped inputs.
- **Compute type for compare**: `kCompare` derives its compute type from the first operand's type (inputs are the arithmetic type; output is `PRED`).
- **Reduce disabled for non-GEMM fusions**: `kReduce` (including rank-preserving reduction lowering) is now rejected with `UnimplementedError` when the fusion has no gemm/conv adapter; reduce support is unchanged for GEMM/conv fusions. Variadic (tuple-shaped) reduce remains unsupported everywhere.

### Autotuner integration

`IsSupportedCudnnFusion` in `xla/backends/gpu/autotuner/cudnn.cc` is extended to accept non-GEMM fusions that aren't already tagged with kCustom when `xla_gpu_cudnn_non_gemm_fusion_level >= 1`, enabling autotuning over cuDNN/Native emitter and other backends for these fusions.

### New flag

```
--xla_gpu_cudnn_non_gemm_fusion_level=<int>
  0: Disabled (default)
  1: Compile pointwise fusions with cuDNN
```

### Tests

`xla/backends/gpu/codegen/cudnn_test.cc` has broad coverage including: pointwise elementwise ops, broadcasts, logical ops, clamp, reciprocal (`f32`), concat, slice, reshape/bitcast, and various dtype combinations, with test names/traits reorganized and shapes reduced to keep runtime down. `cudnn_non_gemm_fusion_rewriter_test.cc` covers the rewriter pass itself, including the multi-concatenate skip case.

display_title: [ROCm] [CUDA] PR 3/3: Skip re-recording unchanged collectives in command buffers

head_commit.message:
[ROCm] [CUDA] Skip re-recording unchanged collectives in command buffers

- With COLLECTIVES and non-persistent buffer allocations, Initialize
  re-records every command buffer that holds a collective on every
  execution, so that all participants record their collectives together.
- New flag --xla_gpu_command_buffer_skip_unchanged_collectives (default
  off): when every participant is in this process, the participants agree
  through a host rendezvous and record again only if one of them has to:
  not warmed up, not recorded yet, profiling, or a buffer of these
  collectives moved. The flag is a field of CommandBufferThunkOptions.
- CountLocalParticipants in collective_params is shared by gpu_executable
  and the vote. CommandBufferThunk shares one per-allocation check between
  the update and the vote, and the vote stops at the first moved buffer.

display_title: Build the HloModule of a GpuExecutable on demand

head_commit.message:
Build the HloModule of a GpuExecutable on demand

We want to stop building the `HloModule` when we load a `GpuExecutable` from
its serialized form, because the executable doesn't need it to run. But some
code (profiling, debugging) still needs the module, so it has to be built on
demand.

So this change replaces `GpuExecutable::Params::debug_module` with
`Params::hlo_module`, a variant that holds either nothing, the module, or the
serialized module (`HloModuleProtoWithConfig`). With a serialized module the
executable passes a factory to the new `Executable` constructor, and
`Executable::GetOrCreateHloModule` builds the module with it the first time
someone needs it. After that `has_module()` returns true. The built module gets
the `pjrt_id` of the serialized module as its unique id, so profiler
annotations and debug info refer to the same id before and after the module is
built. Therefore `Create` rejects a serialized module without a non-negative
`pjrt_id`.

Building the module is observable on purpose, so that we can find the code
that still needs it: It's logged with the reason (and with a stack trace at
`VLOG(1)`), it increments the new counter
`/xla/gpu/hlo_module_materializations{reason}`, and the new flag
`--xla_gpu_experimental_fail_on_lazy_hlo_module_materialization` turns it into
a `FailedPrecondition` error (if it's set at compile time or at load time).

Only modules that are there at construction are registered with the
`XlaDebugInfoManager`, so the destructor now remembers whether it has to
unregister the module instead of looking at `has_module()`. And `ToProto` now
looks at the module only once, so that the serialized module and constants are
consistent even if the module gets built concurrently. If the module hasn't been
built yet, `ToProto` writes the serialized module, which the executable shares
with the factory.

Serialized executables don't carry a `pjrt_id`. So once `FromProto` passes the
serialized module instead of building it, it has to assign a fresh id first. I
left a TODO for that in `FromProto`.

Nothing creates executables with a serialized module yet (`FromProto` still
builds the module), so this doesn't change any behaviour.

The tests are in the new CPU-only target
`//xla/service/gpu:gpu_executable_hlo_module_test` so that the concurrency
test can also run with TSAN.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1012082361

display_title: Ignore element size and memory space in CommonPjRtClient::Delinearize.

head_commit.message:
Ignore element size and memory space in CommonPjRtClient::Delinearize.

XLA `Literal` shapes always clear `element_size_in_bits` to 0 (storing sub-byte elements unpacked at 1 byte per element) and use the default `memory_space`, whereas PJRT buffer shapes carry packed `element_size_in_bits` (for example, 4 for `S4`/`U4` or 2 for `S2`/`U2`) and the buffer's `memory_space` (such as `Layout::kHostMemorySpace`). Comparing `literal_layout != shape.layout()` in `CommonPjRtClient::Delinearize` therefore always evaluated `need_transpose = true` for every sub-byte buffer and every host-memory-space buffer, even when the rest of the layout already matched. For sub-byte transfers, that forced an unnecessary heap allocation and zero-fill of `staged_buffer` at the full unpacked byte size followed by an identity `TransposePlan::Execute` copy on top of `UnpackIntN`, leaving the direct `UnpackIntN` branch unreachable.

Compare layouts in `CommonPjRtClient::Delinearize` with `Layout::Equal().IgnoreElementSize().IgnoreMemorySpace()`, taking the direct unpack or `memcpy` fast path when layouts otherwise match (and guarding `std::memcpy` on 0-byte outputs). On `BM_DelinearizeInt4`, this speeds up `S4` delinearization by 3.1x–3.7x for cache-resident buffers (4 Ki and 1 Mi elements, reaching 31–37 GiB/s) and by 9.7x for 64 Mi-element buffers (48.1 ms to 4.95 ms) by avoiding transient 64 MiB `staged_buffer` page faults and copies.

Tested with unit tests in `//xla/pjrt:common_pjrt_client_test` covering matching default and non-default `minor_to_major` sub-byte layouts, odd-element tail-byte masking, transposed sub-byte layouts, `kHostMemorySpace` buffers (including 0-element spans), and end-to-end `BufferFromHostLiteral` to `ToLiteral` round-trips, alongside `BM_DelinearizeInt4` microbenchmarks.

Dependent small fusions are often dominated by fixed kernel launch and scheduling overheads when run as separate kernels. Executing dependent fusions as sequential phases of a single Hopper (SM90+) thread-block-cluster kernel separated by cluster barriers pays that launch overhead only once while exchanging intermediate results via DRAM or caches. Note that `ThreadBlockSpecializedFusion` (cl/1012181303) combines independent fusions across disjoint CTAs and is complementary.

Current limitations (to be lifted in follow-up CLs):

* Only straight-line chains of `kLoop` fusions
* Nested fusion must fit a single thread block cluster
* No buffer aliasing with fusion outputs

display_title: Allow building the HloModule of an Executable on demand

head_commit.message:
Allow building the HloModule of an Executable on demand

`Executable` takes its `HloModule` in the constructor and never changes it.
But we want `GpuExecutable` to build its module from a serialized module only
when something needs it (e.g. the profiler), and once that happened the module
should be visible through `has_module()`, `module()` and `shared_module()` like
any other module.

So this change adds a second `Executable` constructor that takes an
`HloModuleFactory` instead of a module, and `Executable::GetOrCreateHloModule`,
which returns the module and builds it with the factory if needed. The factory
is called at most once, even with concurrent callers, and if it fails every
later call returns the same error. After a successful build `has_module()`
returns true. The accessors do an acquire load of a raw pointer to the module
and only look at the `shared_ptr` once that pointer is non-null (it never
changes after that), so the read path doesn't need a lock. (We can't use
`std::atomic<std::shared_ptr>` since XLA still has to build with C++17.)

The lazy state lives in a separate heap allocation, so executables that get
their module in the constructor don't pay for it and behave exactly as before.
There is also a new `Executable(std::nullptr_t)` constructor, since
`Executable(nullptr)` would be ambiguous otherwise.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1012180323

head_commit.message:
PR #52257: [ROCm profiler] Keep each kernel's own kernel_details in a graph launch

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52257

## Problem

when running through command buffers (HIP graphs), one `hipGraphLaunch` yields one HIP API record and one dispatch record per graph node, all under one correlation id. In the trace, every kernel of that launch shows the same `kernel_details`: the registers, shared memory, grid and block of whichever dispatch record reached the buffer first. That first kernel's row is correct, however, the rest kernels' details are incorrect.

📝 Summary of Changes

- Remove both copies. `KernelEvent` already fills each activity row from its own dispatch record, and `kernel_details` is exported only for activity kernel rows. The host row still takes `device_id` and `stream_id` from the first record.
- Remove the activity-side `memset_info` copy. The API row never carries it, and the tracer emits no Memset activities today.
- `MultipleActivitiesPerCorrelationIdAllExported` now gives its three kernels distinct grids and checks that each exported row keeps its own grid. On the old code, kernel_b and kernel_c show kernel_a's `grid:4,1,1`.

`rocm_collector_test` and `rocm_tracer_test_amdgpu_any` pass locally and under `--config=rocm_ci_hermetic` on MI355X.

🎯 Justification

| Measure | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| HIP graph of 3 fixed-shape kernels, 5 launches per run: rows whose details differ from their own launch | 10 of 15, in 3 of 3 runs | 0, in 6 of 6 runs |
| JAX step with `--xla_gpu_autotune_level=0`, 5 graph launches of 3 kernels: distinct `kernel_details` per launch | 1, in 3 of 3 runs | 3, in 3 of 3 runs |
| MaxText llama2-7b training, 8 GPUs: graph kernels with one `regs`/`static_shared` across all their rows | 14 of 142 (1 run) | 142 of 142 (2 runs) |
| Same run: graph kernels that also launch outside a graph and match those launches | 0 of 8 | 8 of 8 |
| Blit kernel grid / block | `0,0,0 / 0,0,0` | `1,1,1 / 512,1,1` |

🚀 Kind of Contribution
Please remove what does not apply: 🐛 Bug Fix

99c67a6473b1ffc52b4f3224a4846428e4cf0459 by cj401-amd <chunyjin@amd.com>:

[ROCm profiler] Keep each kernel's own kernel_details in a graph launch

One hipGraphLaunch yields many kernel-dispatch records under one correlation
id. ApiActivityInfoExchange copied the kernel_info of the first record to
arrive onto the HIP API row, then copied that back onto every activity kernel
row with the same correlation id. So every kernel in a graph launch showed the
registers, shared memory, grid and block of whichever record reached the
buffer first.

Two more cases went through the same copy. kernel_info and memcpy_info share a
union, so when a memcpy record arrived first, every kernel row showed the
copy's bytes read as kernel details. And a copy API served by a blit kernel
gave that kernel a zero grid and block, because the API row only received the
first 16 bytes of the kernel's details.

KernelEvent already fills each activity row's kernel_info from its own
dispatch record and code-object symbol, and kernel_details is exported only
for activity kernel rows, so the activity loop no longer overwrites it. The
API loop no longer copies kernel_info onto the HIP API row either: that row
does not export it, and the first record may not be a kernel, in which case
the copy read a memcpy's bytes as KernelDetails. The host row still takes
device_id and stream_id from the first record. The activity loop's Memset case
no longer copies memset_info from the API row, which never carries it; the
tracer emits no Memset activities today, so this changes nothing yet.

MultipleActivitiesPerCorrelationIdAllExported now gives its three kernels
distinct grids and checks that each exported row keeps its own.
TestAddKernelEventAndExport now initialises its activity's kernel_info,
which it used to export uninitialised. Both exchange tests stop setting
kernel details on the HIP API event: those never reached the output, and the
API row now carries none.

Merging this change closes #52257

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Reland: Scale intermediate tile sizes by byte width in EstimateNumWarps.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Reland: Scale intermediate tile sizes by byte width in EstimateNumWarps.

`EstimateNumWarps` picks the warp count from the largest padded tile in the fusion. Broadcasts, `iota` and narrow intermediates such as `pred` comparisons feeding a reduction inflate that size by 4x or more, which selects 4-8 warps where 2-4 are faster.

Keep counting operand and root tiles in full, but ignore non-root `broadcast` and `constant` tiles, size non-root `iota` by its extent along `iota_dimension`, and scale other non-root array tiles by `min(element_bytes, 4) / 4`. `EstimateNumWarps` now takes the `HloFusionAdaptor` to tell fusion operands from intermediates.

This relands cl/1008957649 (rolled back in cl/1010131399) without its `blocks_per_core` change to the compute-time estimate. That change regressed an inference benchmark by 1.5-1.66x.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1012020591
