head_commit.message:
Skip unaffected JAX CI builds using Bazel query

CPU JAX presubmit builds currently run whenever any non-test C++ file in XLA changes, even if the change only affects GPU compiler passes. We cannot filter by directory name alone because CPU `jaxlib` depends on several data structures and protos defined under `xla/service/gpu/` and `xla/backends/gpu/`.

Therefore this change uses `bazel query` in `build_tools/ci/change_detector.py` to check whether the modified XLA files are in the transitive dependency graph of the JAX build's targets. If none of the modified files are reachable, the JAX build is skipped.

Also:

1. Enable `--remote_download_minimal` on `JAX_WINDOWS_X86_CPU_GITHUB_ACTIONS` in `build_tools/ci/build.py` to match the Linux JAX builds.

display_title: Store runtime metadata in GpuExecutable

head_commit.message:
Store runtime metadata in GpuExecutable

`GpuExecutable` read the runtime `DebugOptions`, the `partition_size` and the
static device assignment from the `HloModuleConfig` of its `HloModule`. Without
a module it silently fell back to hard-coded values. That ties execution to the
module, which we want to stop building for loaded executables.

So this change stores the three values in `GpuExecutable` instead. For JIT
compiled executables they come from the module config, and `FromProto` reads
them straight from `hlo_module_with_config.config` (including the fallback to
`HloModuleProto.device_assignment` that `HloModule::CreateFromProto` does). The
execution path, the buffer allocator, the module annotations and the static
device assignment check now use the stored values, and
`CommandBufferConversionPass` gets the `partition_size` explicitly. The
per-flag precedence between compile-time and load-time options is unchanged and
now documented next to the new members.

The stored options are a copy taken in `GpuExecutable::Create`, while before
every execution read the live module config. I found no code that changes the
debug options of an executable's module after `Create`, so this doesn't change
anything in practice.

Executables without a module config behave differently now. They ran without
any debug options, so the execution code fell back to hard-coded values. Most of
them match the flag defaults, but one doesn't: without options the communication
streams didn't get the highest priority, while
`xla_gpu_enable_highest_priority_async_stream` defaults to true. Now these
executables use the options passed to `GpuExecutable::Create`. So they get
highest-priority communication streams, and runtime flags set by the user (e.g.
NCCL channels or rendezvous timeouts) take effect for them, like they already do
for executables with a module. That affects two paths:

1. JIT compilation with `xla_embed_hlo_module=false`, where `GpuCompiler`
   passes the compile-time options of the module.
2. `GpuExecutable::FromProto` with a proto without `hlo_module_with_config`
   (which is what such an executable serializes to), where these are the
   load-time options.

Executables with a module behave as before.

Also remove the unused `module_id` parameter of `ExecuteThunksImpl`.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1012070565

head_commit.message:
PR #51671: XLA:GPU: Sanitize constants on all execution threads

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/51671

📝 Summary of Changes
Run GPU constant-name sanitization across all HLO execution threads instead of only the main execution thread.

This ensures constants inside async computations created by explicit stream annotations are sanitized before GPU code generation. A regression test was added for a constant inside a stream-annotated call.

🎯 Justification
`ExplicitStreamAnnotationAsyncWrapper` creates async computations on the parallel execution thread, while `SanitizeConstantNames` previously ran only on the main execution thread.

As a result, constants in these async computations could reach GPU code generation with unsanitized names and trigger the ConstantNameToGlobalName DCHECK.

This change runs constant-name sanitization across all execution threads while keeping the remaining post-scheduling passes scoped to the main execution thread.

Fixes #50829

🚀 Kind of Contribution
Please remove what does not apply: 🐛 Bug Fix

📊 Benchmark (for Performance Improvements)
NA

🧪 Unit Tests:
Added `GpuCompilerTest.SanitizesConstantNamesInParallelExecutionThread`, which compiles an HLO containing a constant inside a stream-annotated call through the GPU compiler pipeline.

🧪 Execution Tests:
No execution tests added.

head_commit.message:
PR #52149: [XLA:GPU][oneAPI] Refactor oneDNN matmul

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52149

This PR refactors sycl_matmul_utils.{h.cc} to build the oneDNN matmul descriptor in one place and make the code more readable.
The SYCL matmul code built the oneDNN matmul primitive descriptor in two separate places:

- CreateMatMulPrimDescFromGemmConfig, used at compile time bySyclGemmWorkspacePass to decide how many bytes of workspace to reserve.
- DoOnednnGemm, used at run time to actually do the matmul.

This change makes both paths call one shared function, CreateOneDnnMatMulPrimDesc, so they can no longer drift apart.

- Added 2 new test-cases to exercise Bias followed by ReLU/Approx-GeLU post-ops

display_title: [XLA] Reject index_vector_dim batching dims in gather/scatter expansion

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Reject index_vector_dim batching dims in gather/scatter expansion

ExpandIndexVectorIntoOperandSpace builds one index per explicit
batching dim of the gather or scatter indices.
GenerateExplicitBatchDimIndices skips index_vector_dim, so when
start_indices_batching_dims (or scatter_indices_batching_dims)
contains index_vector_dim, the matching entry stays null and is passed
to MakeBroadcastHlo, which dereferences it. HloVerifier accepts such
modules, both with an explicit index_vector_dim and with the implicit
trailing one.

Return InvalidArgument in that case. Add GatherExpander and
ScatterExpander tests for both cases, plus controls with the batching
dim next to index_vector_dim.

display_title: PR #48875: [XLA] Fix trivial reduce-window simplification with negative window padding

head_commit.message:
PR #48875: [XLA] Fix trivial reduce-window simplification with negative window padding

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/48875

## 📝 Summary of Changes

`AlgebraicSimplifier` rewrites a `reduce-window` with a 1x...x1 window (no stride, dilation or reversal, add/min/max reducer) into a plain elementwise op on the operand, wrapped in a `pad` when the window has padding. The wrapper was only built when some padding amount was positive. Window padding can also be negative (a crop), which changes the shape just like positive padding does. With only negative padding the rewrite replaced a `f32[7,4]` reduce-window with a `f32[8,4]` add, `ReplaceInstruction` failed its shape RET_CHECK, and the simplifier turned that into a fatal CHECK, so compilation aborted the process.

This change applies the positive padding amounts with a `pad` and the negative amounts with a `slice`, so the replacement always has the reduce-window's shape. It deliberately never emits a `pad` with negative edge padding: such a pad would be seen by consumers later in the same simplifier sweep, and the pad-into-reduce-window / pad-into-convolution folds in this file assume non-negative edge padding, so a crop feeding a padded reduce-window would have been folded into a wrong net padding (#48715 covers that fold). The mixed-sign case, which previously produced a negative pad and relied on `HandlePad` to turn it into a slice, now takes the same pad-plus-slice path. For the module from the issue the whole thing simplifies to `slice(x)`.

Tests added to `algebraic_simplifier_test.cc`: `TrivialReduceWindowWithNegativePad` (aborts the test binary before this change), `TrivialReduceWindowWithMixedSignPad`, and `TrivialReduceWindowWithNegativePadFeedingPaddedReduceWindow` (checks the consumer keeps its own padding).

## 🎯 Justification

Fixes #48719. Compile-time process abort on valid HLO (negative reduce-window padding is documented and reachable from `lax.reduce_window`). The pass is shared by all backends.

## 🚀 Kind of Contribution

🐛 Bug Fix

## 🧪 Unit Tests:

`bazel test //xla/hlo/transforms/simplifiers:algebraic_simplifier_test`

## 🧪 Execution Tests:

None added (pass-level fix). Verified locally on CPU that the issue's module and the crop-feeding-a-padded-reduce-window module compile and produce the expected values.
Copybara import of the project:

9084afa58b0af7090de1af90957c62ea4bfd8926 by Stanislav Bardyuk <sbardyuk@google.com>:

[XLA] Fix trivial reduce-window simplification with negative window padding

The AlgebraicSimplifier rewrite of a reduce-window with a 1x...x1 window
into an elementwise op only padded the result when some window padding
amount was positive. Negative window padding (a crop) also changes the
shape, so a window with only negative padding produced a replacement of
the wrong shape and ReplaceInstruction CHECK-failed, aborting compilation.

Apply positive padding amounts with a pad and negative amounts with a
slice. The rewrite no longer emits pads with negative edge padding, which
the pad-into-reduce-window and pad-into-convolution folds do not handle.

Fixes #48719.

--
8e49526621a668880fc6c37e7e5783b77a538fa6 by Stanislav Bardyuk <sbardyuk@google.com>:

Emit the crop slice before the pad in the trivial reduce-window rewrite

Create the slice for the negative window padding directly on the
elementwise op and put the pad for the positive padding on top of it, so
that slice-sinking passes can move the slice into the elementwise op.

--
bbda2f1733814d3a64a57f18371852a3c1eb1da6 by Stanislav Bardyuk <sbardyuk@google.com>:

Handle window padding that crops beyond the dimension in the trivial reduce-window rewrite

A negative padding larger than the dimension (e.g. f32[2] with pad=-3_2)
is valid HLO as long as the output size stays non-negative, but the slice
emitted for the crop then has start > limit and the simplifier fails.
No operand element reaches the output in that case, so replace the
reduce-window with a broadcast of the init value instead.

--
aacf2e98b1b640d3544ca3fbdefbd2afc652c45a by Stanislav Bardyuk <sbardyuk@google.com>:

Skip the trivial reduce-window rewrite for negatively padded dynamic dimensions

A negative window padding crops relative to the runtime size of a dynamic
dimension, which the static slice emitted by the rewrite cannot express, and
an unbounded dimension would reach the slice with the INT64_MIN size sentinel.
Bail out of the rewrite in that case. Also treat a crop of exactly the
dimension size as fully cropped so it folds directly to broadcast(init).

--
305022f3c7322f0cd593997b81715ea9ed473d15 by Stanislav Bardyuk <sbardyuk@google.com>:

Bail out of the trivial reduce-window rewrite for any dynamic operand with a crop

The slice that applies a negative window padding covers every dimension of
the operand, so a dynamic dimension without a crop still breaks it. Check the
whole operand shape once before slicing instead of only the cropped dimension.

Merging this change closes #48875

head_commit.message:
PR #47839: [XLA:GPU] Add cuDNN non-GEMM pointwise fusion support via TensorIR engine

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/47839

## Summary

This PR adds support for lowering non-GEMM HLO pointwise fusions to the cuDNN graph API using the `CUDNN_GENERIC_MEMBOUND_FUSION_TENSOR_IR_ENGINE` (cuDNN's dedicated memory-bound TensorIR engine). The feature is controlled by a new flag `--xla_gpu_cudnn_non_gemm_fusion_level`.

### TensorIR engine selection

For non-GEMM (memory-bound) fusions, `PrepareGraph` in `cudnn_fusion_compiler.cc` sets `force_tensor_ir=true` in `EngineOptions`. In `CudnnGraph::Prepare` (`cuda_dnn.cc`), this deselects engines that report `NUMERICAL_NOTE_TENSOR_CORE` (the CUTLASS FALLBACK engines, eng0-eng2), leaving only `CUDNN_GENERIC_MEMBOUND_FUSION_TENSOR_IR_ENGINE` (eng3). GEMM fusions continue to use the full engine set.

### Extended `cudnn_fusion_compiler.cc`

- **Non-GEMM parameter setup**: Added a parameter-binding path for fusions with no gemm/conv adapter, using `DimensionsAndStrides` directly from the HLO shape.
- **Broadcast lowering**: Fixed same-rank and rank-expanding broadcasts. Non-trivial broadcasts are represented via a logical reshape + pointwise identity so cuDNN sees a full-shape virtual tensor.
- **Logical ops**: `kAnd`, `kOr`, `kNot` now map to cuDNN `LOGICAL_{AND,OR,NOT}` for `PRED`-typed operands (bitwise variants remain unsupported).
- **Clamp fix**: Corrected operand ordering to match XLA semantics: `min(max(value, lower), upper)`.
- **Constant handling**: Extended from scalar-only to any single-element constant (e.g. `s32[1]`, `f32[1,1]`). For non-GEMM/conv fusions, constants are always tagged `COMPILE_TIME_CONST`; GEMM/conv fusions keep the prior behavior of runtime scalar tensors for non-scalar-shaped inputs.
- **Compute type for compare**: `kCompare` derives its compute type from the first operand's type (inputs are the arithmetic type; output is `PRED`).
- **Reduce disabled for non-GEMM fusions**: `kReduce` (including rank-preserving reduction lowering) is now rejected with `UnimplementedError` when the fusion has no gemm/conv adapter; reduce support is unchanged for GEMM/conv fusions. Variadic (tuple-shaped) reduce remains unsupported everywhere.

### Autotuner integration

`IsSupportedCudnnFusion` in `xla/backends/gpu/autotuner/cudnn.cc` is extended to accept non-GEMM fusions that aren't already tagged with kCustom when `xla_gpu_cudnn_non_gemm_fusion_level >= 1`, enabling autotuning over cuDNN/Native emitter and other backends for these fusions.

### New flag

```
--xla_gpu_cudnn_non_gemm_fusion_level=<int>
  0: Disabled (default)
  1: Compile pointwise fusions with cuDNN
```

### Tests

`xla/backends/gpu/codegen/cudnn_test.cc` has broad coverage including: pointwise elementwise ops, broadcasts, logical ops, clamp, reciprocal (`f32`), concat, slice, reshape/bitcast, and various dtype combinations, with test names/traits reorganized and shapes reduced to keep runtime down. `cudnn_non_gemm_fusion_rewriter_test.cc` covers the rewriter pass itself, including the multi-concatenate skip case.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Evict command buffers when a GPU clique is split or destroyed.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Evict command buffers when a GPU clique is split or destroyed.

When a cached GPU clique is abandoned during communicator splitting or
destroyed, any command buffers recorded with resources tied to that clique
become stale. Tie per-clique cleanup state (`CliqueState`) to each acquired
clique via `CollectiveCliques::TieAll(...)` when the command buffer is created.
When any of those cliques are abandoned or destroyed, `~CliqueState()` resets
the command buffer on that device, ensuring stale CUDA graphs are cleaned up
before `ncclCommDestroy` runs and forcing re-capture on the next execution.

[XLA:GPU] Launch the largest buffer of a combined collective in its own group

NCCL orders the calls of a group itself and binds the launch completion event to one call, so the event could fire before other kernels of the collective launched. The largest buffer now runs alone in a second group after the others, so the event marks the whole launch.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Forbid fusing reductions into over-broadcasting loop fusions.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Forbid fusing reductions into over-broadcasting loop fusions.

***Problem:*** Priority fusion can fuse a producer containing a low-factor reduction into a `kLoop` consumer that reads it through several slices, broadcasts it, or uses it as a per-thread scalar operand (`dynamic-slice`/`dynamic-update-slice` indices, `pad` value), so the loop emitter recomputes the whole reduction redundantly for every thread of a much larger output domain.

***Solution:*** `PriorityFusionQueue::CanFuseWithNativeEmitter` now forbids such a fusion when the consumer's iteration domain exceeds the reduction's smallest input by at least 256K elements and its total reduction evaluations reach at least 16x that input size, so low-ratio cases such as same-shape softmax stages and small-batch consumers stay fused.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1013585144

display_title: PR #48875: [XLA] Fix trivial reduce-window simplification with negative window padding

head_commit.message:
PR #48875: [XLA] Fix trivial reduce-window simplification with negative window padding

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/48875

## 📝 Summary of Changes

`AlgebraicSimplifier` rewrites a `reduce-window` with a 1x...x1 window (no stride, dilation or reversal, add/min/max reducer) into a plain elementwise op on the operand, wrapped in a `pad` when the window has padding. The wrapper was only built when some padding amount was positive. Window padding can also be negative (a crop), which changes the shape just like positive padding does. With only negative padding the rewrite replaced a `f32[7,4]` reduce-window with a `f32[8,4]` add, `ReplaceInstruction` failed its shape RET_CHECK, and the simplifier turned that into a fatal CHECK, so compilation aborted the process.

This change applies the positive padding amounts with a `pad` and the negative amounts with a `slice`, so the replacement always has the reduce-window's shape. It deliberately never emits a `pad` with negative edge padding: such a pad would be seen by consumers later in the same simplifier sweep, and the pad-into-reduce-window / pad-into-convolution folds in this file assume non-negative edge padding, so a crop feeding a padded reduce-window would have been folded into a wrong net padding (#48715 covers that fold). The mixed-sign case, which previously produced a negative pad and relied on `HandlePad` to turn it into a slice, now takes the same pad-plus-slice path. For the module from the issue the whole thing simplifies to `slice(x)`.

Tests added to `algebraic_simplifier_test.cc`: `TrivialReduceWindowWithNegativePad` (aborts the test binary before this change), `TrivialReduceWindowWithMixedSignPad`, and `TrivialReduceWindowWithNegativePadFeedingPaddedReduceWindow` (checks the consumer keeps its own padding).

## 🎯 Justification

Fixes #48719. Compile-time process abort on valid HLO (negative reduce-window padding is documented and reachable from `lax.reduce_window`). The pass is shared by all backends.

## 🚀 Kind of Contribution

🐛 Bug Fix

## 🧪 Unit Tests:

`bazel test //xla/hlo/transforms/simplifiers:algebraic_simplifier_test`

## 🧪 Execution Tests:

None added (pass-level fix). Verified locally on CPU that the issue's module and the crop-feeding-a-padded-reduce-window module compile and produce the expected values.

9084afa58b0af7090de1af90957c62ea4bfd8926 by Stanislav Bardyuk <sbardyuk@google.com>:

[XLA] Fix trivial reduce-window simplification with negative window padding

The AlgebraicSimplifier rewrite of a reduce-window with a 1x...x1 window
into an elementwise op only padded the result when some window padding
amount was positive. Negative window padding (a crop) also changes the
shape, so a window with only negative padding produced a replacement of
the wrong shape and ReplaceInstruction CHECK-failed, aborting compilation.

Apply positive padding amounts with a pad and negative amounts with a
slice. The rewrite no longer emits pads with negative edge padding, which
the pad-into-reduce-window and pad-into-convolution folds do not handle.

Fixes #48719.

--
8e49526621a668880fc6c37e7e5783b77a538fa6 by Stanislav Bardyuk <sbardyuk@google.com>:

Emit the crop slice before the pad in the trivial reduce-window rewrite

Create the slice for the negative window padding directly on the
elementwise op and put the pad for the positive padding on top of it, so
that slice-sinking passes can move the slice into the elementwise op.

--
bbda2f1733814d3a64a57f18371852a3c1eb1da6 by Stanislav Bardyuk <sbardyuk@google.com>:

Handle window padding that crops beyond the dimension in the trivial reduce-window rewrite

A negative padding larger than the dimension (e.g. f32[2] with pad=-3_2)
is valid HLO as long as the output size stays non-negative, but the slice
emitted for the crop then has start > limit and the simplifier fails.
No operand element reaches the output in that case, so replace the
reduce-window with a broadcast of the init value instead.

--
aacf2e98b1b640d3544ca3fbdefbd2afc652c45a by Stanislav Bardyuk <sbardyuk@google.com>:

Skip the trivial reduce-window rewrite for negatively padded dynamic dimensions

A negative window padding crops relative to the runtime size of a dynamic
dimension, which the static slice emitted by the rewrite cannot express, and
an unbounded dimension would reach the slice with the INT64_MIN size sentinel.
Bail out of the rewrite in that case. Also treat a crop of exactly the
dimension size as fully cropped so it folds directly to broadcast(init).

--
305022f3c7322f0cd593997b81715ea9ed473d15 by Stanislav Bardyuk <sbardyuk@google.com>:

Bail out of the trivial reduce-window rewrite for any dynamic operand with a crop

The slice that applies a negative window padding covers every dimension of
the operand, so a dynamic dimension without a crop still breaks it. Check the
whole operand shape once before slicing instead of only the cropped dimension.

Merging this change closes #48875

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Accept float-normalized add combiners in Triton scans and share the check with CanTritonHandleScan.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Accept float-normalized add combiners in Triton scans and share the check with CanTritonHandleScan.

Add `IsAdditiveScanCombiner`. It requires a combiner with two parameters of the output element type whose root is `tuple(x, x)`, where `x` is `add(p0, p1)` or `convert(add(convert(p0), convert(p1)))`. Use it in:

- `EmitScan`, which now accepts the `convert` form. This fixes `bf16` scans on pre-Hopper GPUs (e.g. A100, A6000), where `GpuFloatSupport` normalizes `bf16` `kAdd` and `FloatNormalization` wraps it in `kConvert`s. `EmitScan` now also rejects combiners whose carry differs from the output, because the lowering derives the carry from the output, and combiners whose add operands are not the parameters.
- `CanTritonHandleScan`, which accepted any associative combiner supported by Triton, so `ScanRewriterTriton` could create scan fusions that `EmitScan` rejects (e.g. a max scan). `FusionBlockLevelRewriter` checks the fusion after `FloatNormalization`, so `CanTritonHandleScan` must accept the `convert` form as well.

Make the combiners in `ScanSupportTest` valid `tuple(add, add)` roots, and check the forbid reason in each negative test. Add support tests for non-additive combiners, a device test for the `convert` form, and a lit test that compiles a `bf16` cumulative sum to a Triton scan kernel.

`IsSupportedCudnnFusion` in `xla/backends/gpu/autotuner/cudnn.cc` is extended to accept non-GEMM fusions that aren't already tagged with kCustom when `xla_gpu_cudnn_non_gemm_fusion_level >= 1`, enabling autotuning over cuDNN/Native emitter and other backends for these fusions.

### New flag

```
--xla_gpu_cudnn_non_gemm_fusion_level=<int>
  0: Disabled (default)
  1: Compile pointwise fusions with cuDNN
```

`xla/backends/gpu/codegen/cudnn_test.cc` has broad coverage including: pointwise elementwise ops, broadcasts, logical ops, clamp, reciprocal (`f32`), concat, slice, reshape/bitcast, and various dtype combinations, with test names/traits reorganized and shapes reduced to keep runtime down. `cudnn_non_gemm_fusion_rewriter_test.cc` covers the rewriter pass itself, including the multi-concatenate skip case.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Remove disabled autotune backends when no backend list is set.

`ConfigAssignerPass::GetEnabledBackends` removes disabled backends from `xla_gpu_experimental_autotune_backends` and passes the result on as an allowlist, where an empty list means all backends. DebugOptions that don't start from `DefaultDebugOptionsIgnoringFlags()`, e.g. ones serialized before it populated the list, can leave the list empty. Then nothing is removed, and disabled backends stay enabled, e.g. `TENSOR_IR` without `xla_gpu_experimental_enable_tensor_ir`.

Populate an empty list with all backends, like the defaults do, before removing the disabled ones. All existing rules (binary libraries, emitters, Triton, TensorIR) then apply to an empty list too.

[TF] Switch TensorFlow default build to Bzlmod and sync MODULE.bazel.

Following the Bazel 8.8.2 upgrade, enable `--enable_bzlmod` and `--noenable_workspace` by default in TensorFlow while adding `--config=workspace` as a fallback configuration and retaining `--config=bzlmod` for backward compatibility with existing CI scripts. Also set `--experimental_repository_downloader_retries=5` to reduce external repository fetch flakes in CI, and remove the obsolete `use_dlls` flags from `common:win_clang_base` (as `protobuf` 33.6 under Bzlmod no longer defines `build_defs:use_dlls` and `third_party/absl:build_dll.patch` is no longer needed).

In `MODULE.bazel` and third-party Bzlmod extensions:
- Register the hermetic SYCL and ROCm C++ toolchains from `rules_ml_toolchain`, sync the CUDA, NCCL, NVSHMEM, SYCL, local sysroot, and `libdrm` module extensions and XLA third-party repositories with XLA's `MODULE.bazel` and `workspace2.bzl`, and align the root BCR module declarations (`pybind11_bazel` 3.0.0, `apple_support` 2.8.0, `rules_swift` 2.9.0, `googletest` 1.18.0, and `highway` 1.4.0).
- Configure `googleapis_ext`, `maven`, and Bzlmod Java repositories (`generated_rule_name` in `java_repos.bzl` and Guava/JSR305/ErrorProne repos), alias `@system_python//:python_headers` to `rules_python`'s hermetic headers in `bazel9.patch`, and update `nvidia_wheel_deps` and `code_check_full.bats` for Bzlmod.

Also extract a pure-MLIR `IfrtIrTestBase` (`ifrt_ir_test_base.{h,cc}`) with `mlir_context_`, dialect registration, and `LoadFromSource` as the base of `IfrtIrLoadedExecutableTestBase` and `IfrtInterfacesTest`.

display_title: Switch Linux builds from libstdc++ (C++17) to statically linked libc++ (C++20)

head_commit.message:
Switch Linux builds from libstdc++ (C++17) to statically linked libc++ (C++20)

This update enables testing Tensorflow with statically linked libc++ (LLVM 22) on Linux (x86_64 and aarch64), adds C++20 support.

Official Linux wheels are now built with Clang and `libc++` instead of `libstdc++` , and introduce Manylinux 2.27 compatible wheels. Out-of-tree C++ custom ops targeting official Linux wheels must be compiled with Clang and `-stdlib=libc++` (now returned automatically by `tf.sysconfig.get_compile_flags()`).

Patches:
third_party/tensorflow/third_party/tf_runtime/invoke_result.patch
Replaces std::result_of_t (removed in C++20 libc++) with std::invoke_result_t in @tf_runtime, which is pinned to an external GitHub commit in OSS builds.

third_party/tensorflow/third_party/com_google_highway/build.patch
Why needed: Updates hunk context lines for the com_google_highway bump from 1.3.0 to 1.4.0.

Other changes
third_party/tensorflow/core/kernels/cwise_ops.h
In libc++, std::function has a different size and alignment on the x86_64 host (sizeof = 48, alignof = 16 due to 16-byte long double alignment in std::aligned_storage) than on the NVPTX64 CUDA device (sizeof = 32, alignof = 8). Because the comparison functors in cwise_ops.h inherited from std::function<bool(T, T)> and are embedded by value inside Eigen::TensorEvaluator CUDA kernel arguments, this host/device layout mismatch shifted the offsets of the GPU tensor pointers in the kernel parameter buffer and caused CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS crashes. Replacing : std::function<bool(T, T)> with using result_type = bool; keeps the typedef required by Eigen while making the functors stateless 1-byte structs with identical layout on host and device.

third_party/tensorflow/core/util/gpu_device_functions.h
In CUDA device code, Eigen::half (__half) and Eigen::bfloat16 (__nv_bfloat16) have explicit Eigen::numext::bit_cast specializations to and from uint16_t (using CUDA intrinsics like __half_as_ushort and __ushort_as_bfloat16), but no direct specialization between Eigen::half and Eigen::bfloat16. Without a direct specialization, Eigen::numext::bit_cast<Eigen::bfloat16>(Eigen::half) falls back to memcpy between two different class types in device registers, which NVCC's device compiler (cicc) optimizes into 0—causing GpuAtomicAdd on bfloat16 (e.g., in gather_op_test_gpu) to produce all zeros. Routing the conversion through uint16_t in detail::GpuAtomicCasHelper uses the explicit CUDA intrinsic specializations instead of the broken memcpy fallback.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1013493861

display_title: Merge adjacent sub-axes in GetMeshAxesPartitionGroupsAcrossTargetDims.

head_commit.message:
Merge adjacent sub-axes in GetMeshAxesPartitionGroupsAcrossTargetDims.

When `TryMultipleSourceTargetDims` fuses an `all-to-all` across multiple target dimensions whose shardings hold contiguous sub-axes of the same mesh axis (such as `model:(1)4` on `target_dims[0]` and `model:(4)2` on `target_dims[1]`), `GetMeshAxesPartitionGroupsAcrossTargetDims` concatenates the per-dimension `AxisRef` spans without merging adjacent sub-axes. Passing that unmerged vector to `MeshAxesReplicaGroupList` fails the `ValidateSpanOfAxes` check (`Adjacent axes in dimension sharding can be merged`), which broke SPMD partitioning when `sdy-optimize-collectives` emits sub-axis `all-to-all` decompositions.

Call `MergeAxes(axis_refs, mesh)` before constructing `MeshAxesReplicaGroupList` in `GetMeshAxesPartitionGroupsAcrossTargetDims`, matching `GetMeshAxesPartitionGroupsForReplication`.

head_commit.message:
Prune unused constrained MakeFakeLiteral template instantiations.

Separate unconstrained fake-literal generation from test-fuzzing value constraints in `xla/literal_util.cc` so binaries calling the 3-argument `MakeFakeLiteral` API do not instantiate or link constrained fuzzing paths across all 32 XLA array element types.

* Parameterize `MakeFakeLiteralImpl` and its floating-point, complex, and integral population helpers on `bool kConstrained` so the 3-argument `MakeFakeLiteral` overload omits sorting, deduplication, precision-capping, custom generator, and interval/alignment branches at compile time.
* Pass an `absl::FunctionRef` partition callback to `ParallelPopulateWithEngine` instead of templating it on per-type lambdas, and evaluate `kBitWidth <= 4` with `if constexpr`.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: Evaluate bazel-diff target selection against the checked-out PR merge commit.

head_commit.message:
Evaluate bazel-diff target selection against the checked-out PR merge commit.

GitHub Actions pull request jobs check out a synthetic merge commit of
the PR into the target branch while passing the unmerged PR branch tip
as the comparison head. When the target branch renames or deletes a
test target after the PR branches, computing impacted targets against
the unmerged PR tip emits labels that no longer exist at the checked-out
merge commit, causing Bazel to fail during target pattern parsing. When
HEAD is a merge of the requested PR tip, compare the merge commit
against its target-branch parent instead and fetch that parent shallowly
when needed so target selection matches the workspace graph without
unshallowing clones or triggering false config-skew full runs.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: Handle SliceToDynamic operands laid out unlike the result

head_commit.message:
Handle SliceToDynamic operands laid out unlike the result

Layout assignment doesn't tie the layout of a SliceToDynamic operand to
that of its result. When they differ, such as a column-major operand of
a row-major result:

- The GPU emitter linearized each output index in the output's layout
  but delinearized the result into the operand index in the operand's
  layout, so the dynamic elements came out scrambled, and a square
  result came out transposed. Delinearize in the output's layout, in
  which the dynamic elements are stored densely.
- The CPU emitter read the operand with an index in the output's
  layout, which failed the IrArray shape compatibility check.

Both emitters now read the operand at an index built against the
operand's shape.

Found in tensorflow/tensorflow#128995.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: Wake waiting threads in FIFO order in xla::Semaphore::Acquire.

head_commit.message:
Wake waiting threads in FIFO order in xla::Semaphore::Acquire.

When a multi-model TPU inference server is under heavy concurrency and hits its
max in-flight computation limit (`max_inflight_computations_semaphore_`),
incoming requests block on `xla::Semaphore::Acquire`. Because `Acquire` waited
on `absl::Mutex::LockWhen` without tracking arrival order, releasing capacity
woke arbitrary waiting threads rather than the oldest waiting request, allowing
newly arrived requests to repeatedly jump ahead of older requests and causing
severe tail-latency starvation.

Track blocked callers in an intrusive arrival-order queue on stack-allocated
`CanAcquireArgs` nodes so the earliest satisfiable waiter is woken first.

Tested with `bazel test //xla/pjrt:semaphore_test`.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1014141776

display_title: Prune unused constrained MakeFakeLiteral template instantiations.

head_commit.message:
Prune unused constrained MakeFakeLiteral template instantiations.

Separate unconstrained fake-literal generation from test-fuzzing value constraints in `xla/literal_util.cc` so binaries calling the 3-argument `MakeFakeLiteral` API do not instantiate or link constrained fuzzing paths across all 32 XLA array element types.

* Parameterize `MakeFakeLiteralImpl` and its floating-point, complex, and integral population helpers on `bool kConstrained` so the 3-argument `MakeFakeLiteral` overload omits sorting, deduplication, precision-capping, custom generator, and interval/alignment branches at compile time.
* Pass an `absl::FunctionRef` partition callback to `ParallelPopulateWithEngine` instead of templating it on per-type lambdas, and evaluate `kBitWidth <= 4` with `if constexpr`.

Runtime and memory impact: neutral (`BM_MakeFakeLiteral` across 64x64 to 1024x1024 tensors is statistically unchanged with zero additional heap allocations, as `ParallelPopulateWithEngine` invokes its `FunctionRef` callback once per parallel partition).

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Simplify tile offset indexing map unconditionally.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Simplify tile offset indexing map unconditionally.

***Problem:*** `EmitterContext::EvaluateTilingParameters` only simplifies `offset_indexing_map` when `tile_constraints` is non-empty, leaving redundant schedule constraints in the map domain when `num_tiles` is an exact multiple of `num_tiles_per_pid`.

***Solution:*** Call `offset_indexing_map.Simplify()` unconditionally in `EmitterContext::EvaluateTilingParameters` while keeping `preserve_result_ranges` gated on non-empty `tile_constraints` so redundant domain bounds are canonicalized away without changing result range annotations.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: Wake waiting threads in FIFO order in xla::Semaphore::Acquire.

head_commit.message:
Wake waiting threads in FIFO order in xla::Semaphore::Acquire.

When a multi-model TPU inference server is under heavy concurrency and hits its
max in-flight computation limit (`max_inflight_computations_semaphore_`),
incoming requests block on `xla::Semaphore::Acquire`. Because `Acquire` waited
on `absl::Mutex::LockWhen` without tracking arrival order, releasing capacity
woke arbitrary waiting threads rather than the oldest waiting request, allowing
newly arrived requests to repeatedly jump ahead of older requests and causing
severe tail-latency starvation.

Track blocked callers in an intrusive arrival-order queue on stack-allocated
`CanAcquireArgs` nodes so the earliest satisfiable waiter is woken first.

Tested with `bazel test //xla/pjrt:semaphore_test`.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1014141776

head_commit.message:
Add GPU platform config registry, slice-spec topology helpers, and SKU validation in XLA:GPU

Downstream runtimes currently maintain separate tables mapping GPU platform names, short aliases (`h100`, `gb300`, `vr200`), and runtime SKU device strings (`"NVIDIA GB300 Max-Q"`, `"NVIDIA Graphics Device"`, `"NVIDIA B300 SXM6 AC"`, `"Tesla P100-PCIE-16GB"`) to per-host GPU counts, Multi-Node NVLink domain sizes, and human-readable device kinds alongside XLA:GPU's embedded target configs.

Add `xla::GpuPlatformConfig`, `GetSupportedGpuPlatformConfigs`, `GetGpuPlatformConfig`, `GetGpuTopologyForSliceSpec`, and `GetGpuDeviceKind` in `xla/service/gpu_topology` so callers can resolve platform aliases and SKU device strings and derive slice topologies directly from XLA:GPU.

Add `xla::gpu::ValidateSupportedGpuTopology` and normalize registered SKU variants to their canonical platform device description in `IsCompatibleWithTargetTopology` (retaining `CompatibleGpuPair` for cross-board pairs such as `B200` / `GB200` and `B300` / `GB300`) so new GPU platforms and SKUs can be onboarded in XLA:GPU without downstream changes.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Propagate XTile tile constraints to elide concat bounds masks.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Propagate XTile tile constraints to elide concat bounds masks.

***Problem:*** `EvaluateTilingParameters` ignores the branch-specific offset constraints that `SymbolicTileAnalysis` records on `concatenate` operand tiles, so bounds checks see the unconstrained offset domain of all branches and emit unnecessary per-element masks on tile-aligned operand loads.

***Solution:*** Add the tile constraints to the offset indexing map, simplify it, and preserve its result ranges on `xla.apply_indexing` so branch-narrowed offsets elide the masks, while `EmitConcatenate` yields a zero tile whenever the concatenate offset is not provably in range (e.g. under a surrounding `pad`).

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1014206339

name: CI ROCm
display_title: [jax-buildcop] [XLA:Python] Fix SocketServer shutdown race leaving PjRtClient alive on recv-thread

head_commit.message:
[jax-buildcop] [XLA:Python] Fix SocketServer shutdown race leaving PjRtClient alive on recv-thread

In `SocketNetworkState::~SocketNetworkState()`, `connections_->list.erase(connection_it_)` notified `SocketServer::WaitForQuiesce()` on the main thread before member destructors destroyed `bulk_transport_`, `dests_`, and `table_`. As a result, `SocketBulkTransportFactory::BlockingShutdown()` could observe `t.use_count() > 1` on `RecvThreadState` while `event-loop-thread` was still tearing down `SocketNetworkState::bulk_transport_`, skipping `t->BlockingShutdown()` and leaving `"recv-thread"` holding the last `std::shared_ptr<xla::PjRtClient>` via `PremappedPjRtBuffer` until process exit.

Reset `start_bulk_transport_`, `bulk_transport_`, `dests_`, `table_`, and `factory_` before erasing `connection_it_` and releasing `connections_->mu`, stop `SocketServer::listener_` in `WaitForQuiesce()`, and clear `listeners_` and `waiting_for_connect` before checking `t.use_count() == 1` in `SocketBulkTransportFactory::BlockingShutdown()`.

display_title: Add two disabled reproduction tests to `xla/backends/profiler/gpu/cupti_tracer_test.cc` (with CUDA graph helpers in `xla/backends/profiler/gpu/cuda_test.h` and `xla/backends/profiler/gpu/cuda_test.cu.cc`) covering CUPTI `cuptiFinalize()` failures when profiling CUDA graphs:

head_commit.message:
Add two disabled reproduction tests to `xla/backends/profiler/gpu/cupti_tracer_test.cc` (with CUDA graph helpers in `xla/backends/profiler/gpu/cuda_test.h` and `xla/backends/profiler/gpu/cuda_test.cu.cc`) covering CUPTI `cuptiFinalize()` failures when profiling CUDA graphs:

1. `CuptiTracerTest.DISABLED_GraphTraceWithCuptiFinalizeCrashesOnPostSessionGraphLaunch`: captures and instantiates a CUDA graph before profiling, launches it during a `CuptiTracer` session with `CUPTI_ACTIVITY_KIND_GRAPH_TRACE` and `cupti_finalize = true`, and launches it again after `Disable()` calls `cuptiFinalize()`, reproducing `cudaErrorIllegalAddress` (700) on the post-session graph launch.
2. `CuptiTracerTest.DISABLED_ConcurrentConditionalGraphUpdateWithCuptiFinalizeFails`: builds a parent CUDA graph containing a conditional IF node (`cudaGraphNodeTypeConditional`) whose body contains a child graph node that is continuously recaptured (`cudaStreamBeginCaptureToGraph`) and updated (`cudaGraphExecChildGraphNodeSetParams`) and launched on a worker thread while `CuptiTracer` runs profiling sessions with `CUPTI_ACTIVITY_KIND_CONCURRENT_KERNEL` (without `CUPTI_ACTIVITY_KIND_GRAPH_TRACE`) and `cupti_finalize = true`, reproducing `cudaErrorIllegalAddress` (700) / `cudaErrorLaunchFailure` (719) or driver lock hangs.

Both tests are prefixed with `DISABLED_` so the test target passes by default in CI, while running manually with `--test_arg=--gunit_also_run_disabled_tests` (or `--test_arg=--gtest_also_run_disabled_tests` in OSS) reproduces the failures.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1014176973

display_title: [jax-buildcop] [XLA:Python] Fix SocketServer shutdown race leaving PjRtClient alive on recv-thread

head_commit.message:
[jax-buildcop] [XLA:Python] Fix SocketServer shutdown race leaving PjRtClient alive on recv-thread

In `SocketNetworkState::~SocketNetworkState()`, `connections_->list.erase(connection_it_)` notified `SocketServer::WaitForQuiesce()` on the main thread before member destructors destroyed `bulk_transport_`, `dests_`, and `table_`. As a result, `SocketBulkTransportFactory::BlockingShutdown()` could observe `t.use_count() > 1` on `RecvThreadState` while `event-loop-thread` was still tearing down `SocketNetworkState::bulk_transport_`, skipping `t->BlockingShutdown()` and leaving `"recv-thread"` holding the last `std::shared_ptr<xla::PjRtClient>` via `PremappedPjRtBuffer` until process exit.

Reset `start_bulk_transport_`, `bulk_transport_`, `dests_`, `table_`, and `factory_` before erasing `connection_it_` and releasing `connections_->mu`, stop `SocketServer::listener_` in `WaitForQuiesce()`, and clear `listeners_` and `waiting_for_connect` before checking `t.use_count() == 1` in `SocketBulkTransportFactory::BlockingShutdown()`.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: [XLA:GPU] Accept float-normalized add combiners in Triton scans and share the check with CanTritonHandleScan.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Accept float-normalized add combiners in Triton scans and share the check with CanTritonHandleScan.

Add `IsAdditiveScanCombiner`. It requires a combiner with two parameters of the output element type whose root is `tuple(x, x)`, where `x` is `add(p0, p1)` or `convert(add(convert(p0), convert(p1)))`. Use it in:

- `EmitScan`, which now accepts the `convert` form. This fixes `bf16` scans on pre-Hopper GPUs (e.g. A100, A6000), where `GpuFloatSupport` normalizes `bf16` `kAdd` and `FloatNormalization` wraps it in `kConvert`s. `EmitScan` now also rejects combiners whose carry differs from the output, because the lowering derives the carry from the output, and combiners whose add operands are not the parameters.
- `CanTritonHandleScan`, which accepted any associative combiner supported by Triton, so `ScanRewriterTriton` could create scan fusions that `EmitScan` rejects (e.g. a max scan). `FusionBlockLevelRewriter` checks the fusion after `FloatNormalization`, so `CanTritonHandleScan` must accept the `convert` form as well.

Make the combiners in `ScanSupportTest` valid `tuple(add, add)` roots, and check the forbid reason in each negative test. Add support tests for non-additive combiners, a device test for the `convert` form, and a lit test that compiles a `bf16` cumulative sum to a Triton scan kernel.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: Wake waiting threads in FIFO order in xla::Semaphore::Acquire.

head_commit.message:
Wake waiting threads in FIFO order in xla::Semaphore::Acquire.

When a multi-model TPU inference server is under heavy concurrency and hits its
max in-flight computation limit (`max_inflight_computations_semaphore_`),
incoming requests block on `xla::Semaphore::Acquire`. Because `Acquire` waited
on `absl::Mutex::LockWhen` without tracking arrival order, releasing capacity
woke arbitrary waiting threads rather than the oldest waiting request, allowing
newly arrived requests to repeatedly jump ahead of older requests and causing
severe tail-latency starvation.

Track blocked callers in an intrusive arrival-order queue on stack-allocated
`CanAcquireArgs` nodes so the earliest satisfiable waiter is woken first.

Tested with `bazel test //xla/pjrt:semaphore_test`.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1014141776

display_title: [XLA] Fold collectives on uniform constants in AlgebraicSimplifier.

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Fold collectives on uniform constants in AlgebraicSimplifier.

`AlgebraicSimplifier` already folds `all-gather`, `all-to-all`, `all-reduce`, and `reduce-scatter` (`min`/`max`/`sum`) when their operand is `broadcast(scalar_constant)`. Extend this to plain uniform `constant` operands—such as scalar (`pred[]`) and single-element (`pred[1]`) constants, which are not canonicalized into broadcasts.

For example, this now folds to `%x` in a single pass:
```
%ar0 = pred[1] all-reduce(pred[1] constant({true})), to_apply=min
%ar1 = pred[]  all-reduce(pred[] reshape(%ar0)), to_apply=min
%out = pred[]  and(%x, %ar1)
```

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Propagate XTile tile constraints to elide concat bounds masks.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Propagate XTile tile constraints to elide concat bounds masks.

***Problem:*** `EvaluateTilingParameters` ignores the branch-specific offset constraints that `SymbolicTileAnalysis` records on `concatenate` operand tiles, so bounds checks see the unconstrained offset domain of all branches and emit unnecessary per-element masks on tile-aligned operand loads.

***Solution:*** Add the tile constraints to the offset indexing map, simplify it, and preserve its result ranges on `xla.apply_indexing` so branch-narrowed offsets elide the masks, while `EmitConcatenate` yields a zero tile whenever the concatenate offset is not provably in range (e.g. under a surrounding `pad`).

display_title: [XLA] Preserve tighter xla.range bounds in ApplyIndexing and folding.

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Preserve tighter xla.range bounds in ApplyIndexing and folding.

***Problem:*** Folding an `xla.apply_indexing` result that is a bare dimension or symbol to its operand drops any `xla.range` that is tighter than the operand's own range, so later range-based simplifications can no longer use that bound.

***Solution:*** Only fold such a result in `ApplyIndexingOp::fold` and `FoldApplyIndexingResults` if the operand's range is contained in the op's `xla.range`, and add an opt-in `preserve_result_ranges` flag to `emitters::ApplyIndexing` that annotates variable results with their domain-derived range.

display_title: Improve `LatencyHidingScheduler` memory-limit reruns in three ways:

head_commit.message:
Improve `LatencyHidingScheduler` memory-limit reruns in three ways:
- Restore the original input schedule (and invalidate `AsyncTracker` caches)
  before every retry so trials differ only in `SchedulerConfig`.
- Evaluate peak non-parameter default-memory-space usage across all rerun modes
  via whole-module `HeapSimulator` (`GlobalDecreasingSizeBestFitHeap` with
  spatial packing) whenever `rerun > 0` and `memory_limit` is finite, capturing
  heap fragmentation and cross-computation aliasing missed by the online
  `MemoryPressureTracker`.
- Retain the earliest trial achieving the lowest `HeapSimulator` peak if later
  retries with tighter `0.9x` limits do not reduce peak heap usage.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: Break ties between ready async-done instructions by data dependency.

head_commit.message:
Break ties between ready async-done instructions by data dependency.

When two supported async-done candidates are otherwise tied in
`ReadySetLt::AIsBetterThanB`, the scheduler falls back to the original
instruction order. For example, when two dependent layers each offload their
result to host, the input order may list the deeper layer's copy-done first,
which delays the earlier layer's offload past the next layer's compute and
completes the offloads in reverse dependency order. For async ops that execute
in order on another core (e.g. SparseCore offloads expressed as
async-start/async-update/async-done chains), the done order also fixes the
issue order, so a reversed done order forces every earlier-produced transfer to
wait behind the last one and clusters all offloads at the end of the program.

Add a `kAsyncDoneDataDependency` tie-breaker before `kOriginalOrder`: find each
done's async start (through any async-updates; the start is the only op of an
async chain with data operands) and collect its data operands, skipping operands
shared by both starts (e.g. common offsets) as well as parameters and constants,
which are available from the start. If a data operand of one start reaches the
other start (via the schedule graph's reachability map), the done transferring
the earlier-produced data completes first in program order. Dones without a
separate start that the `AsyncTracker` supports (e.g. synchronous collectives a
backend schedules as async) and unrelated async-dones are unaffected and keep
their original order.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1014116348

[XLA:GPU] Propagate XTile tile constraints to elide concat bounds masks.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: Add AOT compatibility goldens for single-GPU library thunks

head_commit.message:
Add AOT compatibility goldens for single-GPU library thunks

The XLA:GPU AOT compatibility tests only covered collective and control-flow
thunks, so a serialization break in a library or custom-call thunk went
unnoticed. This adds more tests, one single-GPU target per thunk, each with one minimal HLO op: `triangular_solve_aot_test`,
`fft_aot_test`, `convolution_aot_test`, `cublas_lt_matmul_aot_test`,
`ffi_custom_call_aot_test` and `rng_seed_aot_test`.

Each thunk depends on a different library or emitter, and golden versions are
per target, so one target per thunk keeps a library change (e.g. a cuBLAS
version bump) from creating new golden versions for unrelated thunks.

The cuBLASLt heuristic's pick depends on the CUDA version the test is built with
(on B200, algo_id 16 at 13.2 and 23 at 12.8), so `cublas_lt_matmul_aot_test`
pins the algorithm per arch and requires the runtime to rebuild it exactly. Its
golden then does not depend on the CUDA version, and a runtime that can no
longer rebuild an older algorithm fails the test instead of falling back to the
heuristic.

The GPU test parameter helpers move from `collective_aot_test_base` into
`gpu_aot_test_params`, because the single-GPU targets have no collectives.

starting `ExecutionProfile`, `ProfilerInterface` sessions, scoped logging
timers, and `RunningOptions::total_run_time`, add

earlier parameters before fanning out from the primary device, and skip

through host DRAM).

floating-point and narrow (<= 8-bit) integral static arrays of at least
`FakeArgumentsOptions::min_cached_argument_bytes` (scaled between 64 KiB and
16 MiB in `FunctionalHloRunner` based on module parameter footprint) so
predicates, >= 16-bit integer index/routing tensors, small per-layer router
matrices on large modules, and constrained index arrays stay distinct across
parameters, and advance `std::minstd_rand0` by the exact per-tensor step count
so uncached parameters match `cache_arguments = false`.

display_title: [IFRT IR] Generalize IfrtMergeCopiesAndReshardsPass to IfrtMergeOpsPass and support merging BitcastArrays

head_commit.message:
[IFRT IR] Generalize IfrtMergeCopiesAndReshardsPass to IfrtMergeOpsPass and support merging BitcastArrays

`IfrtMergeCopiesAndReshardsPass` maintained separate key-hashing and rewriting paths for `ifrt.CopyArrays` and single-output `ifrt.Reshard` operations over raw `mlir::Operation*`, leaving multi-array `ifrt.Reshard` and compatible `ifrt.BitcastArrays` operations unmerged and dispatched individually at runtime.

Rename the pass to `IfrtMergeOpsPass` (`-ifrt-merge-ops`) and unify base merge-key hashing, grouping, and merged-op rewriting across `IfrtPairwiseArrayOpInterface` operations (`ifrt.CopyArrays`, `ifrt.Reshard`, and `ifrt.BitcastArrays`). Compatible uniform-device operations that share source and destination devices, donation semantics, and discardable attributes are now merged into a single batched operation while preventing donated operations that share an input array from being merged together.

Merging non-pairwise `ifrt.RemapArrays` operations remains unsupported, but can be supported later if needed.

display_title: Break ties between ready async-done instructions by data dependency.

head_commit.message:
Break ties between ready async-done instructions by data dependency.

When two supported async-done candidates are otherwise tied in
`ReadySetLt::AIsBetterThanB`, the scheduler falls back to the original
instruction order. For example, when two dependent layers each offload their
result to host, the input order may list the deeper layer's copy-done first,
which delays the earlier layer's offload past the next layer's compute and
completes the offloads in reverse dependency order. For async ops that execute
in order on another core (e.g. SparseCore offloads expressed as
async-start/async-update/async-done chains), the done order also fixes the
issue order, so a reversed done order forces every earlier-produced transfer to
wait behind the last one and clusters all offloads at the end of the program.

Add a `kAsyncDoneDataDependency` tie-breaker before `kOriginalOrder`: find each
done's async start (through any async-updates; the start is the only op of an
async chain with data operands) and collect its data operands, skipping operands
shared by both starts (e.g. common offsets) as well as parameters and constants,
which are available from the start. If a data operand of one start reaches the
other start (via the schedule graph's reachability map), the done transferring
the earlier-produced data completes first in program order. Dones without a
separate start that the `AsyncTracker` supports (e.g. synchronous collectives a
backend schedules as async) and unrelated async-dones are unaffected and keep
their original order.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Accept float-normalized add combiners in Triton scans and share the check with CanTritonHandleScan.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Accept float-normalized add combiners in Triton scans and share the check with CanTritonHandleScan.

Add `IsAdditiveScanCombiner`. It requires a combiner with two parameters of the output element type whose root is `tuple(x, x)`, where `x` is `add(p0, p1)` or `convert(add(convert(p0), convert(p1)))`. Use it in:

- `EmitScan`, which now accepts the `convert` form. This fixes `bf16` scans on pre-Hopper GPUs (e.g. A100, A6000), where `GpuFloatSupport` normalizes `bf16` `kAdd` and `FloatNormalization` wraps it in `kConvert`s. `EmitScan` now also rejects combiners whose carry differs from the output, because the lowering derives the carry from the output, and combiners whose add operands are not the parameters.
- `CanTritonHandleScan`, which accepted any associative combiner supported by Triton, so `ScanRewriterTriton` could create scan fusions that `EmitScan` rejects (e.g. a max scan). `FusionBlockLevelRewriter` checks the fusion after `FloatNormalization`, so `CanTritonHandleScan` must accept the `convert` form as well.

Make the combiners in `ScanSupportTest` valid `tuple(add, add)` roots, and check the forbid reason in each negative test. Add support tests for non-additive combiners, a device test for the `convert` form, and a lit test that compiles a `bf16` cumulative sum to a Triton scan kernel.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Use xla.range bounds of tile offsets in Triton mask elision.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Use xla.range bounds of tile offsets in Triton mask elision.

***Problem:*** `EmitGeneric` records the program ID bounds as an `xla.range` attribute on the tile ID argument so that they survive folding of identity `xla.apply_indexing` ops, but `XTileEntryToTriton` drops that attribute and Triton mask elision only derives offset ranges from `arith.constant` and `xla.apply_indexing` ops (and additionally requires tile-size divisibility), so the annotation is dead and masks stay on provably in-bounds tiles.

***Solution:*** Forward the tile ID's `xla.range` attribute onto the lowered `arith.index_cast` in `XTileEntryToTriton`, and query `xla::GetRange` with feasibility and overflow-safe bounds checks in `IsGuaranteedInBounds` and `TritonXlaCollapseContiguousMinorDimsPass`, eliding a mask exactly when every accessed element `offset + i * stride` is provably within the dimension (which makes the extra divisibility checks redundant).

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1014070104

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Propagate XTile tile constraints to elide concat bounds masks.

***Problem:*** `EvaluateTilingParameters` ignores the branch-specific offset constraints that `SymbolicTileAnalysis` records on `concatenate` operand tiles, so bounds checks see the unconstrained offset domain of all branches and emit unnecessary per-element masks on tile-aligned operand loads.

***Solution:*** Add the tile constraints to the offset indexing map, simplify it, and preserve its result ranges on `xla.apply_indexing` so branch-narrowed offsets elide the masks, while `EmitConcatenate` yields a zero tile whenever the concatenate offset is not provably in range (e.g. under a surrounding `pad`).

display_title: [XLA] Preserve tighter xla.range bounds in ApplyIndexing and folding.

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Preserve tighter xla.range bounds in ApplyIndexing and folding.

***Problem:*** Folding an `xla.apply_indexing` result that is a bare dimension or symbol to its operand drops any `xla.range` that is tighter than the operand's own range, so later range-based simplifications can no longer use that bound.

***Solution:*** Only fold such a result in `ApplyIndexingOp::fold` and `FoldApplyIndexingResults` if the operand's range is contained in the op's `xla.range`, and add an opt-in `preserve_result_ranges` flag to `emitters::ApplyIndexing` that annotates variable results with their domain-derived range.

display_title: [IFRT IR] Generalize IfrtMergeCopiesAndReshardsPass to IfrtMergeOpsPass and support merging BitcastArrays

head_commit.message:
[IFRT IR] Generalize IfrtMergeCopiesAndReshardsPass to IfrtMergeOpsPass and support merging BitcastArrays

`IfrtMergeCopiesAndReshardsPass` maintained separate key-hashing and rewriting paths for `ifrt.CopyArrays` and single-output `ifrt.Reshard` operations over raw `mlir::Operation*`, leaving multi-array `ifrt.Reshard` and compatible `ifrt.BitcastArrays` operations unmerged and dispatched individually at runtime.

Rename the pass to `IfrtMergeOpsPass` (`-ifrt-merge-ops`) and unify base merge-key hashing, grouping, and merged-op rewriting across `IfrtPairwiseArrayOpInterface` operations (`ifrt.CopyArrays`, `ifrt.Reshard`, and `ifrt.BitcastArrays`). Compatible uniform-device operations that share source and destination devices, donation semantics, and discardable attributes are now merged into a single batched operation while preventing donated operations that share an input array from being merged together.

Merging non-pairwise `ifrt.RemapArrays` operations remains unsupported, but can be supported later if needed.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1013471611

display_title: PR #51671: XLA:GPU: Sanitize constants on all execution threads

head_commit.message:
PR #51671: XLA:GPU: Sanitize constants on all execution threads

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/51671

📝 Summary of Changes
Run GPU constant-name sanitization across all HLO execution threads instead of only the main execution thread.

This ensures constants inside async computations created by explicit stream annotations are sanitized before GPU code generation. A regression test was added for a constant inside a stream-annotated call.

🎯 Justification
`ExplicitStreamAnnotationAsyncWrapper` creates async computations on the parallel execution thread, while `SanitizeConstantNames` previously ran only on the main execution thread.

As a result, constants in these async computations could reach GPU code generation with unsanitized names and trigger the ConstantNameToGlobalName DCHECK.

This change runs constant-name sanitization across all execution threads while keeping the remaining post-scheduling passes scoped to the main execution thread.

Fixes #50829

📊 Benchmark (for Performance Improvements)
NA

🧪 Unit Tests:
Added `GpuCompilerTest.SanitizesConstantNamesInParallelExecutionThread`, which compiles an HLO containing a constant inside a stream-annotated call through the GPU compiler pipeline.

display_title: [IFRT IR] Forward control inputs when `replaceWithKeptOutputs` drops all array outputs

head_commit.message:
[IFRT IR] Forward control inputs when `replaceWithKeptOutputs` drops all array outputs

Dropping all array outputs via `replaceWithKeptOutputs` while `control_output` still had users fell through to `cloneWithKeptOutputs` with zero kept outputs, constructing an empty op op that failed MLIR verification (e.g. `Reshard` and `CopyArrays` ops require at least one input array). Calling `cloneWithKeptOutputs` directly with an all-false `keep` mask exhibited the same failure mode.

Updating `replaceWithKeptOutputs` to forward the op's incoming `control_inputs` (with deduplication across zero, single, or multiple control dependencies) to all users of `control_output` before erasing the op preserves transitive execution ordering without leaving behind invalid zero-input array ops, while `cloneWithKeptOutputs` now returns `nullptr` when `keep.none()`.

display_title: Add AOT compatibility goldens for single-GPU library thunks

head_commit.message:
Add AOT compatibility goldens for single-GPU library thunks

The XLA:GPU AOT compatibility tests only covered collective and control-flow
thunks, so a serialization break in a library or custom-call thunk went
unnoticed. This adds more tests, one single-GPU target per thunk, each with one minimal HLO op: `triangular_solve_aot_test`,
`fft_aot_test`, `convolution_aot_test`, `cublas_lt_matmul_aot_test`,
`ffi_custom_call_aot_test` and `rng_seed_aot_test`.

Each thunk depends on a different library or emitter, and golden versions are
per target, so one target per thunk keeps a library change (e.g. a cuBLAS
version bump) from creating new golden versions for unrelated thunks.

The cuBLASLt heuristic's pick depends on the CUDA version the test is built with
(on B200, algo_id 16 at 13.2 and 23 at 12.8), so `cublas_lt_matmul_aot_test`
pins the algorithm per arch and requires the runtime to rebuild it exactly. Its
golden then does not depend on the CUDA version, and a runtime that can no
longer rebuild an older algorithm fails the test instead of falling back to the
heuristic.

The GPU test parameter helpers move from `collective_aot_test_base` into
`gpu_aot_test_params`, because the single-GPU targets have no collectives.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1010721809

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Disable buffer sharing for phased block-cluster fusions.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Disable buffer sharing for phased block-cluster fusions.

`PhasedBlockClusterFusion` (cl/1013683054) executes multiple nested fusions sequentially inside a single Hopper thread-block-cluster kernel. Without an explicit `GpuAliasInfo` rule, `BufferAssigner` falls back to `FusionCanShareBufferHint` and may reuse a shared outer operand's buffer for an earlier phase's output slice, either failing slice-aliasing checks or overwriting input data still needed by a later phase.

Return `false` from `GpuAliasInfo::MayAlias` for `__phased_block_cluster` fusions so phase outputs are allocated in buffers disjoint from outer operands, and enable execution coverage for shared outer operands across phases.

display_title: [XLA] Saturate 32-bit clamp bound when folding dynamic-slice of iota

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Saturate 32-bit clamp bound when folding dynamic-slice of iota

In `AlgebraicSimplifierVisitor::HandleDynamicSlice`
(`xla/hlo/transforms/simplifiers/algebraic_simplifier.cc`), folding a
1D `dynamic-slice` of an `iota` (or scaled `iota`) clamps the scalar
`S32`/`U32` start index to `[0, iota_size - 1]` by narrowing
`iota_size - 1` directly to `int32_t` or `uint32_t`. When
`iota_size - 1` exceeds `INT32_MAX` (for `S32` indices) or `UINT32_MAX`
(for `U32` indices), the upper bound wraps around and corrupts the
clamped index.

Saturate the clamp upper bound to the maximum representable value of
`index_type`, which is equivalent across all 32-bit index values, and
add symbolic >32-bit `S32` and `U32` unit tests.

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Preserve tighter xla.range bounds in ApplyIndexing and folding.

***Problem:*** Folding an `xla.apply_indexing` result that is a bare dimension or symbol to its operand drops any `xla.range` that is tighter than the operand's own range, so later range-based simplifications can no longer use that bound.

***Solution:*** Only fold such a result in `ApplyIndexingOp::fold` and `FoldApplyIndexingResults` if the operand's range is contained in the op's `xla.range`, and add an opt-in `preserve_result_ranges` flag to `emitters::ApplyIndexing` that annotates variable results with their domain-derived range.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Use xla.range bounds of tile offsets in Triton mask elision.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Use xla.range bounds of tile offsets in Triton mask elision.

***Problem:*** `EmitGeneric` records the program ID bounds as an `xla.range` attribute on the tile ID argument so that they survive folding of identity `xla.apply_indexing` ops, but `XTileEntryToTriton` drops that attribute and Triton mask elision only derives offset ranges from `arith.constant` and `xla.apply_indexing` ops (and additionally requires tile-size divisibility), so the annotation is dead and masks stay on provably in-bounds tiles.

***Solution:*** Forward the tile ID's `xla.range` attribute onto the lowered `arith.index_cast` in `XTileEntryToTriton`, and query `xla::GetRange` with feasibility and overflow-safe bounds checks in `IsGuaranteedInBounds` and `TritonXlaCollapseContiguousMinorDimsPass`, eliding a mask exactly when every accessed element `offset + i * stride` is provably within the dimension (which makes the extra divisibility checks redundant).

display_title: [IFRT IR] Forward control inputs when `replaceWithKeptOutputs` drops all array outputs

head_commit.message:
[IFRT IR] Forward control inputs when `replaceWithKeptOutputs` drops all array outputs

Dropping all array outputs via `replaceWithKeptOutputs` while `control_output` still had users fell through to `cloneWithKeptOutputs` with zero kept outputs, constructing an empty op op that failed MLIR verification (e.g. `Reshard` and `CopyArrays` ops require at least one input array). Calling `cloneWithKeptOutputs` directly with an all-false `keep` mask exhibited the same failure mode.

Updating `replaceWithKeptOutputs` to forward the op's incoming `control_inputs` (with deduplication across zero, single, or multiple control dependencies) to all users of `control_output` before erasing the op preserves transitive execution ordering without leaving behind invalid zero-input array ops, while `cloneWithKeptOutputs` now returns `nullptr` when `keep.none()`.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: Break ties between ready async-done instructions by data dependency.

head_commit.message:
Break ties between ready async-done instructions by data dependency.

When two supported async-done candidates are otherwise tied in
`ReadySetLt::AIsBetterThanB`, the scheduler falls back to the original
instruction order. For example, when two dependent layers each offload their
result to host, the input order may list the deeper layer's copy-done first,
which delays the earlier layer's offload past the next layer's compute and
completes the offloads in reverse dependency order. For async ops that execute
in order on another core (e.g. SparseCore offloads expressed as
async-start/async-update/async-done chains), the done order also fixes the
issue order, so a reversed done order forces every earlier-produced transfer to
wait behind the last one and clusters all offloads at the end of the program.

Add a `kAsyncDoneDataDependency` tie-breaker before `kOriginalOrder`: find each
done's async start (through any async-updates; the start is the only op of an
async chain with data operands) and collect its data operands, skipping operands
shared by both starts (e.g. common offsets) as well as parameters and constants,
which are available from the start. If a data operand of one start reaches the
other start (via the schedule graph's reachability map), the done transferring
the earlier-produced data completes first in program order. Dones without a
separate start that the `AsyncTracker` supports (e.g. synchronous collectives a
backend schedules as async) and unrelated async-dones are unaffected and keep
their original order.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1004167907

display_title: Add ClearExecutionState hook to PjRtLoadedExecutable

head_commit.message:
Add ClearExecutionState hook to PjRtLoadedExecutable

When workloads alternate distinct compiled executables on the same devices,
mutable runtime execution state (such as loaded program handles and dynamic TPU
host or device program stacks) can remain allocated while an executable is
idle between phases.

Add a virtual `PjRtLoadedExecutable::ClearExecutionState()` hook in
`xla/pjrt/pjrt_client.h` (defaulting to `absl::OkStatus()`), along with
`PjRtExecutableLoadState::ClearExecutionState()` in
`xla/pjrt/raw_pjrt_client.h` and forwarding in `CommonPjRtLoadedExecutable`
in `xla/pjrt/common_pjrt_client.h`, to release mutable execution resources
while keeping the compiled executable alive for lazy reload on subsequent
`Execute()` calls.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Use xla.range bounds of tile offsets in Triton mask elision.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Use xla.range bounds of tile offsets in Triton mask elision.

***Problem:*** `EmitGeneric` records the program ID bounds as an `xla.range` attribute on the tile ID argument so that they survive folding of identity `xla.apply_indexing` ops, but `XTileEntryToTriton` drops that attribute and Triton mask elision only derives offset ranges from `arith.constant` and `xla.apply_indexing` ops (and additionally requires tile-size divisibility), so the annotation is dead and masks stay on provably in-bounds tiles.

***Solution:*** Forward the tile ID's `xla.range` attribute onto the lowered `arith.index_cast` in `XTileEntryToTriton`, and query `xla::GetRange` with feasibility and overflow-safe bounds checks in `IsGuaranteedInBounds` and `TritonXlaCollapseContiguousMinorDimsPass`, eliding a mask exactly when every accessed element `offset + i * stride` is provably within the dimension (which makes the extra divisibility checks redundant).

[XLA] Preserve tighter xla.range bounds in ApplyIndexing and folding.

***Problem:*** Folding an `xla.apply_indexing` result that is a bare dimension or symbol to its operand drops any `xla.range` that is tighter than the operand's own range, so later range-based simplifications can no longer use that bound.

display_title: Own constant content when the HloModule is not embedded

head_commit.message:
Own constant content when the HloModule is not embedded

Non-scalar constants are not emitted as initializers in the LLVM IR. Instead the executable keeps their content and copies it to the device on the first execution. That content is a `DenseDataIntermediate` which aliases the literal of the constant instruction in the HloModule. With `CompileOptions::embed_hlo_module=false`, `GpuCompiler::RunBackend` doesn't move the module into the `GpuExecutable`, so the module (and with it the literal) gets destroyed at the end of `RunBackend` and the constants point to freed memory. This went unnoticed so far because the only users of that option (the autotuner and the Triton numerics verifier) compile clones that share their literals with a source module that stays alive.

So this change makes the constants own a copy of their content in `RunBackend`, but only if the module doesn't get embedded. I made the decision there because that's the place that decides to drop the module. The default path (module embedded) keeps aliasing the literals, so there is no extra copy and no additional memory use. The new `DenseDataIntermediate::ToOwned()` only copies aliased data, so sub-byte constants (which are already packed into an owned buffer) don't get copied a second time.

There are two new tests in `xla/service/gpu/gpu_compiler_test.cc`. The first one compiles a module with an f32 and an s4 constant without embedding it, makes sure the module is gone, and then checks the constant contents and the result of an execution. Without the fix it reports a heap-use-after-free under ASAN. The second one doesn't need ASAN: it checks that the constant content aliases the module's literal if and only if the module gets embedded, which also pins the no-copy behavior of the default path.

display_title: Build the HloModule of a GpuExecutable on demand

head_commit.message:
Build the HloModule of a GpuExecutable on demand

We want to stop building the `HloModule` when we load a `GpuExecutable` from
its serialized form, because the executable doesn't need it to run. But some
code (profiling, debugging) still needs the module, so it has to be built on
demand.

So this change replaces `GpuExecutable::Params::debug_module` with
`Params::hlo_module`, a variant that holds either nothing, the module, or the
serialized module (`HloModuleProtoWithConfig`). With a serialized module the
executable passes a factory to the new `Executable` constructor, and
`Executable::GetOrCreateHloModule` builds the module with it the first time
someone needs it. After that `has_module()` returns true. The built module gets
the `pjrt_id` of the serialized module as its unique id, so profiler
annotations and debug info refer to the same id before and after the module is
built. Therefore `Create` rejects a serialized module without a non-negative
`pjrt_id`.

Building the module is observable on purpose, so that we can find the code
that still needs it: It's logged with the reason (and with a stack trace at
`VLOG(1)`), it increments the new counter
`/xla/gpu/hlo_module_materializations{reason}`, and the new flag
`--xla_gpu_experimental_fail_on_lazy_hlo_module_materialization` turns it into
a `FailedPrecondition` error (if it's set at compile time or at load time).

Only modules that are there at construction are registered with the
`XlaDebugInfoManager`, so the destructor now remembers whether it has to
unregister the module instead of looking at `has_module()`. And `ToProto` now
looks at the module only once, so that the serialized module and constants are
consistent even if the module gets built concurrently. If the module hasn't been
built yet, `ToProto` writes the serialized module, which the executable shares
with the factory.

Serialized executables don't carry a `pjrt_id`. So once `FromProto` passes the
serialized module instead of building it, it has to assign a fresh id first. I
left a TODO for that in `FromProto`.

Nothing creates executables with a serialized module yet (`FromProto` still
builds the module), so this doesn't change any behaviour.

The tests are in the new CPU-only target
`//xla/service/gpu:gpu_executable_hlo_module_test` so that the concurrency
test can also run with TSAN.

display_title: Serve PJRT layouts and shardings without the HLO module

head_commit.message:
Serve PJRT layouts and shardings without the HLO module

Once a `StreamExecutorExecutable` is loaded, PJRT reads the parameter and output layouts, the SPMD shardings, the memory kinds and the output shapes from the optimized HLO module. For XLA:GPU that means the module has to exist, even though the `GpuExecutable` already knows the entry computation layout and the result shape.

So this change makes `GpuExecutable` also store the SPMD parameter and output shardings at creation, the same way it stores the entry computation layout: from the module if there is one, else from the serialized module that it keeps, else from the compiler (for `embed_hlo_module=false`). A loaded `StreamExecutorExecutable` with a metadata provider then takes the layouts, the output shapes and the memory kinds from the `Executable`, and the shardings from the provider. Executables without a provider (JIT through `PjRtStreamExecutorClient` and other backends) keep reading the module.

Nothing changes while the module is present. The new tests check that all values match the ones derived from the module (including tuple outputs, aliasing, host memory outputs and an SPMD program with two partitions) and that the overrides never ask the provider for the module. There is also a test that the peak memory sizes computed from the serialized module match the ones computed from the in-memory module.

display_title: Fix 32-bit integer overflow when sharding large iota and arange arrays.

head_commit.message:
Fix 32-bit integer overflow when sharding large iota and arange arrays.

When sharding an `iota` (such as `jnp.arange`) across multiple devices, XLA's SPMD partitioner previously computed each shard's starting offset in 32-bit signed integers before converting to the output type. For ranges whose shard size or starting offset exceeded 2^31 - 1, this overflowed and produced negative offsets even for 64-bit outputs.

Build sharded `iota` offsets directly in the `iota` element type via `MakePartitionOffsets`.

Fixes https://github.com/jax-ml/jax/issues/35896

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Accept float-normalized add combiners in Triton scans and share the check with CanTritonHandleScan.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Accept float-normalized add combiners in Triton scans and share the check with CanTritonHandleScan.

Add `IsAdditiveScanCombiner`. It requires a combiner with two parameters of the output element type whose root is `tuple(x, x)`, where `x` is `add(p0, p1)` or `convert(add(convert(p0), convert(p1)))`. Use it in:

- `EmitScan`, which now accepts the `convert` form. This fixes `bf16` scans on pre-Hopper GPUs (e.g. A100, A6000), where `GpuFloatSupport` normalizes `bf16` `kAdd` and `FloatNormalization` wraps it in `kConvert`s. `EmitScan` now also rejects combiners whose carry differs from the output, because the lowering derives the carry from the output, and combiners whose add operands are not the parameters.
- `CanTritonHandleScan`, which accepted any associative combiner supported by Triton, so `ScanRewriterTriton` could create scan fusions that `EmitScan` rejects (e.g. a max scan). `FusionBlockLevelRewriter` checks the fusion after `FloatNormalization`, so `CanTritonHandleScan` must accept the `convert` form as well.

Make the combiners in `ScanSupportTest` valid `tuple(add, add)` roots, and check the forbid reason in each negative test. Add support tests for non-additive combiners, a device test for the `convert` form, and a lit test that compiles a `bf16` cumulative sum to a Triton scan kernel.
