display_title: [XLA] Simplify the identity map in ComputeEpilogueInputToOutputIndexing.

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Simplify the identity map in ComputeEpilogueInputToOutputIndexing.

`ComputeEpilogueInputToOutputIndexing` only ran `Simplify()` while walking a
non-trivial hero->root use chain. When the root *is* the hero, the raw
identity map was returned instead. With size-1 dimensions the two forms
differ structurally (`(d0, d1, d2) -> (0, d1, d2)` vs.
`(d0, d1, d2) -> (d0, d1, d2)`) even though they are semantically equal, so
`IndexingMap::operator==` reports them as different.

The multi-output concatenate emitter compares the epilogue indexing of all
roots and fails with

```
RET_CHECK failure (xla/codegen/emitters/concatenate_kernel_emitter.cc:200)
UseConcatenateFusion should have ensured all roots share the same epilogue indexing
```

for a fusion where one root is `divide(concatenate(...), ...)` and the other
root is a bare `concatenate`, as soon as the shapes contain a size-1
dimension.

Simplify the initial identity map so the result is canonical regardless of
the chain length. Adds a unit test for the indexing analysis and a GPU
emitter lit test with the failing fusion.

Fixes https://github.com/EnzymeAD/Reactant.jl/issues/3681

display_title: [IFRT IR] Generalize IfrtMergeCopiesAndReshardsPass to IfrtMergeOpsPass and support merging BitcastArrays

head_commit.message:
[IFRT IR] Generalize IfrtMergeCopiesAndReshardsPass to IfrtMergeOpsPass and support merging BitcastArrays

`IfrtMergeCopiesAndReshardsPass` maintained separate key-hashing and rewriting paths for `ifrt.CopyArrays` and single-output `ifrt.Reshard` operations over raw `mlir::Operation*`, leaving multi-array `ifrt.Reshard` and compatible `ifrt.BitcastArrays` operations unmerged and dispatched individually at runtime.

Rename the pass to `IfrtMergeOpsPass` (`-ifrt-merge-ops`) and unify base merge-key hashing, grouping, and merged-op rewriting across `IfrtPairwiseArrayOpInterface` operations (`ifrt.CopyArrays`, `ifrt.Reshard`, and `ifrt.BitcastArrays`). Compatible uniform-device operations that share source and destination devices, donation semantics, and discardable attributes are now merged into a single batched operation while preventing donated operations that share an input array from being merged together.

Merging non-pairwise `ifrt.RemapArrays` operations remains unsupported, but can be supported later if needed.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1013471611

display_title: Avoid unnecessary heap allocations in HloInstruction::ReplaceAllUsesWithDifferentShape.

head_commit.message:
Avoid unnecessary heap allocations in HloInstruction::ReplaceAllUsesWithDifferentShape.

In the `absl::Span` overload `HloInstruction::ReplaceAllUsesWithDifferentShape(absl::Span<HloInstruction* const>, HloInstruction*)` (`xla/hlo/ir/hlo_instruction.cc`), replace `std::vector<HloInstruction*> users_vector` with `absl::InlinedVector<HloInstruction*, 4> users_vector`. An inline capacity of 4 fits within a single 64-byte cache line on the stack (40 bytes on 64-bit platforms: 4 pointers + 8-byte `InlinedVector` header) and covers typical HLO instruction fanout (1-4 users) without heap allocation while preserving safe iteration when `ReplaceUseWithDifferentShape` mutates `this->users_`.

In the single-argument overload `HloInstruction::ReplaceAllUsesWithDifferentShape(HloInstruction*)`, iterate directly over `users()` without materializing a temporary copy, since `this->users_` is not mutated inside the loop before `users_.Clear()`.

Microbenchmark results (`--benchmark_repetitions=9`, `-c opt`):

| Benchmark | Baseline | Optimized | Delta |
| :--- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `BM_ReplaceAllUsesWithDifferentShape/4` | 294 ns | 211 ns | -28.2% (1.39x) |
| `BM_ReplaceAllUsesWithDifferentShape/16` | 613 ns | 497 ns | -18.9% (1.23x) |

When sharding an `iota` (such as `jnp.arange`) across multiple devices, XLA's SPMD partitioner previously computed each shard's starting offset in 32-bit signed integers before converting to the output type. For ranges whose shard size or starting offset exceeded 2^31 - 1, this overflowed and produced negative offsets even for 64-bit outputs.

Build sharded `iota` offsets directly in the `iota` element type via `MakePartitionOffsets`.

Fixes https://github.com/jax-ml/jax/issues/35896

head_commit.message:
Use Executable accessors in HloRunnerLegacy

HloRunnerLegacy read the input/output alias config and the debug options from `Executable::module()`, which doesn't work for executables that were compiled without an embedded HloModule (`embed_hlo_module=false`) or that will be loaded without one in the future.

So this change reads the alias config through `Executable::input_output_alias_config()`, only updates the entry computation layout if the executable has a module, and falls back to the debug options from the flags if there is no module. Nothing changes for executables that have a module.

The new test runs a GPU executable compiled with `embed_hlo_module=false` through HloRunnerLegacy.

display_title: Fix GPU integer `tf.math.pow` mismatch with CPU/NumPy for exponents >= 64.

head_commit.message:
Fix GPU integer `tf.math.pow` mismatch with CPU/NumPy for exponents >= 64.

Previously, the MLIR-generated GPU `Pow` kernel lowered `stablehlo.power` to a Linalg/SCF exponentiation-by-squaring loop with a hardcoded upper bound of 6 iterations, which only inspected the lowest 6 bits of the exponent (`y % 64`) and discarded bits at positions >= 6. As a result, odd bases with exponents >= 64 (such as `(-47)**66`) and even bases with exponents >= 64 produced incorrect results on GPU compared to CPU and NumPy fixed-width two's-complement wrap-around semantics.

Update the integer `Pow` exponentiation-by-squaring loop upper bound from 6 to the integer element bit-width so all exponent bits are processed.

Fixes #118202

display_title: Load PJRT executables without the HLO module

head_commit.message:
Load PJRT executables without the HLO module

`CommonPjRtClient::LoadInternal` always asked the executable for its HLO module to get the result shape, the parameter shapes and the input/output aliasing. On top of that, `CommonPjRtLoadedExecutable::input_output_alias_config()` asked for the module again on every execution if the executable wasn't compiled asynchronously. For XLA:GPU executables that are loaded from a serialized form that's the only reason the module has to exist, since `GpuExecutable` stores all of this already.

So this change adds `PjRtExecutableLoadState::GetEntryComputationInfo`, which returns these values if the loaded executable can provide them without the module. The default returns nothing, so other backends keep reading the module. The StreamExecutor implementation reads them from the `Executable` if the `StreamExecutorExecutable` has a metadata provider, which is the same condition under which it serves layouts and shardings without the module.

The alias config is now stored in the dispatch info at load time (for both the synchronous and the asynchronous path), so executions never need the module.

Also:

1. Deserialized executables are only dumped (and therefore only need the module) if dumping is enabled for the executable's name. If the build options have no debug options, we still ask for the module, since the dump then uses the module's own debug options.
2. Since the entry computation info is only available after `Preload`, the module is now requested after `Preload` as well. That only changes when an error from `GetHloModule()` is reported.

Nothing changes while the module is present. A new test loads executables with and without the provider through the PJRT client, checks that the dispatch info is the same (including aliasing and a host memory output), and checks that neither loading nor executing asks for the module.

head_commit.message:
[PJRT] Clear PadRealToStatic prefix through tuples and async offloads

TPU `PadRealToStatic` reads a dynamic entry parameter as a compact buffer
without the dynamic-shape metadata prefix; PJRT previously cleared that prefix
only for direct entry-computation users and `CHECK`-failed on tuple-packed
parameters. Resolve the parameter with `HloDataflowAnalysis` through tuples,
calls, and async chains, reject shared readers and output aliases, and apply the
same checks on the MLIR compile path.

display_title: [PJRT] Clear PadRealToStatic prefix through embedded offload dispatchers

head_commit.message:
[PJRT] Clear PadRealToStatic prefix through embedded offload dispatchers

Backend offload compilers can replace the root call of an async-wrapped
computation with an embedded custom-call dispatcher that forwards its operands
positionally, and can share one callee computation across several async chains;
dataflow analysis does not forward values into such embedded computations.
Resolve `PadRealToStatic` parameters through those dispatchers so their
metadata prefix is cleared; the previous entry-only scan skipped offloaded calls
silently.

display_title: [IFRT IR] Forward control inputs when `replaceWithKeptOutputs` drops all array outputs

head_commit.message:
[IFRT IR] Forward control inputs when `replaceWithKeptOutputs` drops all array outputs

Dropping all array outputs via `replaceWithKeptOutputs` while `control_output` still had users fell through to `cloneWithKeptOutputs` with zero kept outputs, constructing an empty op op that failed MLIR verification (e.g. `Reshard` and `CopyArrays` ops require at least one input array). Calling `cloneWithKeptOutputs` directly with an all-false `keep` mask exhibited the same failure mode.

Updating `replaceWithKeptOutputs` to forward the op's incoming `control_inputs` (with deduplication across zero, single, or multiple control dependencies) to all users of `control_output` before erasing the op preserves transitive execution ordering without leaving behind invalid zero-input array ops, while `cloneWithKeptOutputs` now returns `nullptr` when `keep.none()`.

display_title: Move X64Rewriter to run immediately after spatial partitioning.

head_commit.message:
Move X64Rewriter to run immediately after spatial partitioning.

This moves X64Rewriter earlier in the HLO pipeline so it runs immediately after spatial partitioning passes (or after call inlining for non-partitioned modules). Running it after SPMD partitioning ensures partitioners operate on standard 64-bit operations before they are lowered into multi-output/tuple 32-bit operations, avoiding suboptimal fallbacks such as emitting AllGathers instead of AllReduces.

Downstream support added to X64Rewriter for the post-partitioning HLO graph:
- Lower 64-bit AllReduce and ReduceScatter collectives (U64/S64 sum with carry, bitwise ops without carry, and general reductions via AllGather + local reduce fallback).
- Handle SPMD custom calls (X64SplitLow, X64SplitHigh, X64Combine) and pass through internal memory annotations (MoveToHost, MoveToDevice, etc.).
- Support convolutions with 64-bit inputs and 32-bit output.
- Rename Phase 0 pipeline stages and timers from "X64 elimination" to "Pre-SPMD type expansion" and "Pre-SPMD optimizations".
- Skip rewriting 64-bit gathers to one-hot matmuls in GatherOptimizer, preserving them for X64Rewriter.

Also adds end-to-end 64-bit reduce tests to spmd_execution_test and shardy_execution_test to verify numerical correctness and distributed execution on TPU hardware.

display_title: Avoid unnecessary heap allocations in HloInstruction::ReplaceAllUsesWithDifferentShape.

head_commit.message:
Avoid unnecessary heap allocations in HloInstruction::ReplaceAllUsesWithDifferentShape.

In the `absl::Span` overload `HloInstruction::ReplaceAllUsesWithDifferentShape(absl::Span<HloInstruction* const>, HloInstruction*)` (`xla/hlo/ir/hlo_instruction.cc`), replace `std::vector<HloInstruction*> users_vector` with `absl::InlinedVector<HloInstruction*, 4> users_vector`. An inline capacity of 4 fits within a single 64-byte cache line on the stack (40 bytes on 64-bit platforms: 4 pointers + 8-byte `InlinedVector` header) and covers typical HLO instruction fanout (1-4 users) without heap allocation while preserving safe iteration when `ReplaceUseWithDifferentShape` mutates `this->users_`.

In the single-argument overload `HloInstruction::ReplaceAllUsesWithDifferentShape(HloInstruction*)`, iterate directly over `users()` without materializing a temporary copy, since `this->users_` is not mutated inside the loop before `users_.Clear()`.

Microbenchmark results (`--benchmark_repetitions=9`, `-c opt`):

| Benchmark | Baseline | Optimized | Delta |
| :--- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `BM_ReplaceAllUsesWithDifferentShape/4` | 294 ns | 211 ns | -28.2% (1.39x) |
| `BM_ReplaceAllUsesWithDifferentShape/16` | 613 ns | 497 ns | -18.9% (1.23x) |

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Use collective memory space for temporary buffers on fully-sharded modules.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Use collective memory space for temporary buffers on fully-sharded modules.

When temporary buffers are allocated on `BFCAllocator`, other allocations can shift the temporary buffer address across executions and trigger expensive CUDA Graph updates.

Add `--xla_gpu_temp_buffer_use_collective_color` to allocate temporary buffers for fully-sharded modules in the collective memory space, keeping their addresses stable across runs. Also fix `BufferAssignment::CombineTempAllocations` to apply `temp_buffer_color` when there is only a single default-colored temporary allocation.

Placing temp buffer in collective memory space for fully-shared module is safe because temp buffer is symmetrical across all peers.

The only side-affect of this change is that it's enabling NCCL RMA kernels if they are using temp default buffers. However currently NCCL RMA kernels are disabled by default.

display_title: Harden CheckpointReader, BundleReader, TwoLevelIterator, and Block against read errors and corrupt metadata.

head_commit.message:
Harden CheckpointReader, BundleReader, TwoLevelIterator, and Block against read errors and corrupt metadata.

Previously, transient file read errors (such as `DEADLINE_EXCEEDED`) or malformed metadata entries during V2 checkpoint scanning could cause `SIGSEGV` or `SIGABRT` crashes:

- `TwoLevelIterator::Next()`, `key()`, and `value()`, as well as `Block::Iter::Next()`, `key()`, and `value()`, now guard against `!Valid()` instead of dereferencing a null `data_iter_` in release builds.
- `Block::Iter` initializes and resets `value_` to `(data_ + restarts_, 0)` so `NextEntryOffset()` never subtracts `data_` from `nullptr`, validates restart offsets against `restarts_` before forming pointers in `Seek()` and `SeekToRestartPoint()`, and uses 64-bit arithmetic in `DecodeEntry()` to prevent 32-bit unsigned integer overflow when checking `(*non_shared + *value_length)`.
- `BundleReader::status()` now propagates `iter_->status()` when `status_` is OK, and `BundleReader::DebugString()` avoids `CHECK`-crashing on invalid iterator states, unparseable `BundleEntryProto` values, or invalid `TensorShapeProto` entries.
- `CheckpointReader::BuildV2VarMaps()` checks `v2_reader_->Valid()` after `Seek(kHeaderEntryKey)` and `v2_reader_->status()` after each pass, replaces `CHECK(entry.ParseFromString(...))`, `TensorSlice(slice_proto)`, `CHECK(filtered_keys.insert(...).second)`, and `TensorShape(entry.shape())` with status-checked builders (`TensorSlice::BuildTensorSlice` and `TensorShape::BuildTensorShape`), and surfaces `DataLossError` via `TF_Status` when `BuildV2VarMaps()` fails without an underlying reader I/O error.

display_title: [XLA] Simplify the identity map in ComputeEpilogueInputToOutputIndexing.

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Simplify the identity map in ComputeEpilogueInputToOutputIndexing.

`ComputeEpilogueInputToOutputIndexing` only ran `Simplify()` while walking a
non-trivial hero->root use chain. When the root *is* the hero, the raw
identity map was returned instead. With size-1 dimensions the two forms
differ structurally (`(d0, d1, d2) -> (0, d1, d2)` vs.
`(d0, d1, d2) -> (d0, d1, d2)`) even though they are semantically equal, so
`IndexingMap::operator==` reports them as different.

The multi-output concatenate emitter compares the epilogue indexing of all
roots and fails with

```
RET_CHECK failure (xla/codegen/emitters/concatenate_kernel_emitter.cc:200)
UseConcatenateFusion should have ensured all roots share the same epilogue indexing
```

for a fusion where one root is `divide(concatenate(...), ...)` and the other
root is a bare `concatenate`, as soon as the shapes contain a size-1
dimension.

Simplify the initial identity map so the result is canonical regardless of
the chain length. Adds a unit test for the indexing analysis and a GPU
emitter lit test with the failing fusion.

Fixes https://github.com/EnzymeAD/Reactant.jl/issues/3681

display_title: Serve PJRT layouts and shardings without the HLO module

head_commit.message:
Serve PJRT layouts and shardings without the HLO module

Once a `StreamExecutorExecutable` is loaded, PJRT reads the parameter and output layouts, the SPMD shardings, the memory kinds and the output shapes from the optimized HLO module. For XLA:GPU that means the module has to exist, even though the `GpuExecutable` already knows the entry computation layout and the result shape.

So this change makes `GpuExecutable` also store the SPMD parameter and output shardings at creation, the same way it stores the entry computation layout: from the module if there is one, else from the serialized module that it keeps, else from the compiler (for `embed_hlo_module=false`). A loaded `StreamExecutorExecutable` with a metadata provider then takes the layouts, the output shapes and the memory kinds from the `Executable`, and the shardings from the provider. Executables without a provider (JIT through `PjRtStreamExecutorClient` and other backends) keep reading the module.

Nothing changes while the module is present. The new tests check that all values match the ones derived from the module (including tuple outputs, aliasing, host memory outputs and an SPMD program with two partitions) and that the overrides never ask the provider for the module. There is also a test that the peak memory sizes computed from the serialized module match the ones computed from the in-memory module.

display_title: Build the HloModule of a GpuExecutable on demand

head_commit.message:
Build the HloModule of a GpuExecutable on demand

We want to stop building the `HloModule` when we load a `GpuExecutable` from
its serialized form, because the executable doesn't need it to run. But some
code (profiling, debugging) still needs the module, so it has to be built on
demand.

So this change replaces `GpuExecutable::Params::debug_module` with
`Params::hlo_module`, a variant that holds either nothing, the module, or the
serialized module (`HloModuleProtoWithConfig`). With a serialized module the
executable passes a factory to the new `Executable` constructor, and
`Executable::GetOrCreateHloModule` builds the module with it the first time
someone needs it. After that `has_module()` returns true. The built module gets
the `pjrt_id` of the serialized module as its unique id, so profiler
annotations and debug info refer to the same id before and after the module is
built. Therefore `Create` rejects a serialized module without a non-negative
`pjrt_id`.

Building the module is observable on purpose, so that we can find the code
that still needs it: It's logged with the reason (and with a stack trace at
`VLOG(1)`), it increments the new counter
`/xla/gpu/hlo_module_materializations{reason}`, and the new flag
`--xla_gpu_experimental_fail_on_lazy_hlo_module_materialization` turns it into
a `FailedPrecondition` error (if it's set at compile time or at load time).

Only modules that are there at construction are registered with the
`XlaDebugInfoManager`, so the destructor now remembers whether it has to
unregister the module instead of looking at `has_module()`. And `ToProto` now
looks at the module only once, so that the serialized module and constants are
consistent even if the module gets built concurrently. If the module hasn't been
built yet, `ToProto` writes the serialized module, which the executable shares
with the factory.

Serialized executables don't carry a `pjrt_id`. So once `FromProto` passes the
serialized module instead of building it, it has to assign a fresh id first. I
left a TODO for that in `FromProto`.

Nothing creates executables with a serialized module yet (`FromProto` still
builds the module), so this doesn't change any behaviour.

The tests are in the new CPU-only target
`//xla/service/gpu:gpu_executable_hlo_module_test` so that the concurrency
test can also run with TSAN.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: Add AOT compatibility goldens for single-GPU library thunks

head_commit.message:
Add AOT compatibility goldens for single-GPU library thunks

The XLA:GPU AOT compatibility tests only covered collective and control-flow
thunks, so a serialization break in a library or custom-call thunk went
unnoticed. This adds more tests, one single-GPU target per thunk, each with one minimal HLO op: `triangular_solve_aot_test`,
`fft_aot_test`, `convolution_aot_test`, `cublas_lt_matmul_aot_test`,
`ffi_custom_call_aot_test` and `rng_seed_aot_test`.

Each thunk depends on a different library or emitter, and golden versions are
per target, so one target per thunk keeps a library change (e.g. a cuBLAS
version bump) from creating new golden versions for unrelated thunks.

The cuBLASLt heuristic's pick depends on the CUDA version the test is built with
(on B200, algo_id 16 at 13.2 and 23 at 12.8), so `cublas_lt_matmul_aot_test`
pins the algorithm per arch and requires the runtime to rebuild it exactly. Its
golden then does not depend on the CUDA version, and a runtime that can no
longer rebuild an older algorithm fails the test instead of falling back to the
heuristic.

The GPU test parameter helpers move from `collective_aot_test_base` into
`gpu_aot_test_params`, because the single-GPU targets have no collectives.

[XLA:GPU] Fix kScaledDot backend gating for Triton and cuDNN.

Problem:    kScaledDot gating mischecks Triton and cuDNN support, and Triton
            tunes scaled dots that it cannot compile.
Solution:   Gate kScaledDot on Triton and CUDNN_FISSION support, check Triton
            support in TritonBackend, and forbid block-16 scales on Blackwell.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: Allow deserializing cuDNN graphs compiled for GPUs with fewer SMs

head_commit.message:
Allow deserializing cuDNN graphs compiled for GPUs with fewer SMs

cuDNN's handle-based execution plan deserialization requires an exact match on
`multiProcessorCount`, so AOT plans for a smaller-SM SKU or MIG partition fail
to load on a GPU of the same architecture with more SMs.

To support this, we serialize the target's SM count and cuDNN's
`DeviceProperties` JSON into `CudnnThunkProto` at compile time and pass them to
`DnnSupport::DeserializeGraph`. The JSON stays opaque to XLA: when the target
has fewer SMs than the attached GPU (`GpuExecutable` already rejects compute
capability mismatches),
`CudnnSupport::DeserializeGraph` deserializes the compile-time
`DeviceProperties`, finalizes the plan against those properties via
`graph.set_device_properties()`, and runs warmup on the handle (keeping same-SM
loads on the existing handle path).
